## Experiment overview

The reel recommends three external videos about Nasdaq futures scalping. It highlights setups, level-based timing, and live entry/exit examples. It does not itself teach the full rules in those videos, and the cited 70% win-rate claim is not independently verified by the recommendation.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Use this initially as a research-process or comparison protocol. A planning workflow, preference or motivational claim is not itself an OHLCV strategy. A run can evaluate a separately specified baseline only after its signals and risk rules are frozen; no psychological or product claim should become a price signal.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: Recommendations visible in the clip

1. My 1 Easy Scalping Strategy Trading NQ Futures, shown from Futures Scalper, with a 09:30-themed thumbnail.
2. The Easiest Futures Strategy I've Ever Used, shown from Dennis Anthony White, with an NQ-scalping subtitle in the thumbnail/title area.
3. A video titled beginning NQ Futures Scalping Strategy That Actually Works in Live Trading, with Reese Cadavals credited in the visible material. The exact canonical URLs are not supplied by the reel.

### Writeup: How to use the list productively

Additional study suggestions: identify the exact intended video before relying on a similar search result, then record its instrument/contract, session, timeframe, entry, invalidation, target, size, and examples of failure. Distinguish a live market commentary from a complete live account record. Keep each instructor's rules separate before deciding whether any combination is coherent.

## Proposed integration

Create a source-specific adapter for the sequence in the Rules and inputs section, preserving the order in which each illustrated reference and confirmation becomes known. Store candidate, armed, confirmed, expired and invalidated events separately. Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

### Writeup: What remains absent and how to evaluate learning

This source provides no complete entry strategy, indicator settings, stop formula, target method, or test sample. Only the reel URL in list.md is downloaded here; unseen external lessons are not summarized as if reviewed. Once a full method is actually studied, apply its frozen definition to later unseen charts and evaluate all eligible decisions with realistic costs. Three attractive titles and a claimed success percentage cannot establish achievable net results or the suitability of futures scalping for a reader.

# Bearish harami at resistance, structural confirmation, and conflicting stop descriptions

Source: [The Easy Way Trading](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1HAUGet5YZ/). Downloaded duration: 45.266 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The lesson rejects selling a small red candle in isolation. It first locates a large bullish candle and a smaller bearish body inside it at resistance, then waits for evidence that upward structure has weakened. A later retest provides the illustrated short. The small inside body is a warning about momentum, not certainty that a reversal has begun.

## How to reproduce the narrated branch

1. Identify the preceding upward swing sequence and a known resistance/supply area.
2. Observe a large bullish candle followed by a smaller bearish body contained within it. The source's definition is body containment, not necessarily containment of every wick.
3. Wait for price to break the relevant higher low as the spoken structural confirmation.
4. Wait for a return to the small inside candle's area before the illustrated short.
5. The narration describes invalidation above its high and an objective at the demand area where the preceding rally began.

## The caption gives different choices

The saved caption permits a close beneath the harami low or a fifteen-minute bearish structure break, then entry on confirmation or on a retest. It places the stop above the large candle's high and targets lower liquidity. That stop can be materially wider than the small-candle-high wording in the narration. A reproducible version must select the exact confirmation, entry, stop, and target branch before testing; it cannot switch among them after seeing which would have survived.

## Missing rules and evaluation

The displayed example is explicitly XAUUSD on fifteen-minute bars and is labeled a simulated chart. Resistance construction, body tolerance, pivot confirmation, retest depth, stop buffer, size, and expiry are not fully specified. An upward trend can continue after a harami, and a structural break can be a temporary pullback. Compare pattern-only, structure-confirmed, and retest-confirmed variants on later data, preserving their different prices and risks. Include all failed patterns, missed retests, and costs. A closing confirmation must be available before an order is modeled as filled.

## Local evidence and reproducibility

About 0–23s establishes the trend, resistance, and inside body; 23–37s gives the structural break and retest; 37–45s gives the demand-area objective. The caption supplies the alternative confirmation and large-candle stop.

# Volume-profile locations combined with footprint aggression and a possible absorption response

Source: [TradeTracker](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1N7fUuAd83/). Downloaded duration: 62.566 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The speaker uses volume-at-price references to choose where to watch and a footprint display to examine aggressive trade activity there. The key example is buying aggression at resistance without upward progress, described as absorption. That observation can suggest a mismatch between aggressive flow and price response, but the clip does not provide a fully quantified entry or prove who holds the opposing inventory.

## How to reproduce the analysis

1. Choose a profile interval, data source, and binning rule. Mark high-volume nodes, low-volume regions, the highest-volume point of control, and the example 70% value-area edges.
2. Keep the selected profile levels available as-of the decision rather than using a completed future session.
3. At a relevant location, inspect actual footprint data and record aggressive buying/selling according to the provider's classification method.
4. Observe whether price advances in the direction of the aggression or fails to do so.
5. Define a separate confirmation and trade-management policy before treating the observation as an entry.

## Data and terminology limits

Historical volume is not current resting depth or a complete record of positions still held. Point of control is the most active price bin, not an independently established economic fair value. A value area needs a declared construction algorithm; simply selecting the largest noncontiguous bins is not necessarily the same as a conventional contiguous area around point of control. Footprint aggression also depends on trade classification and feed completeness; a candle's up/down volume is not automatically equivalent.

The source does not quantify aggression, failure-to-advance, absorption duration, entry, invalidation, target, size, timeframe, or expiry. A temporary stall can resolve in the original aggression direction, and high/low-volume areas do not all react alike. Test a frozen location-plus-response rule against profile-only and flow-only baselines on later data. Include failed stalls, costs, latency, and data entitlements. # Sweep versus breakout: reaction candles and the manner of approach, with a promised third check absent

Source: [ChartTactix](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/19MdSgWdiE/). Downloaded duration: 82.895 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The speaker contrasts rejection after crossing a prior extreme with continued strong candles beyond it. He then compares an aggressive approach with a slower corrective approach. The introduction promises three confirmations, but this upload only reaches two before it ends. The missing third confirmation is not reconstructed from another source.

## How to apply the two stated observations

1. Mark a prior high or low before price approaches it.
2. After an excursion, observe candle behavior: immediate strong rejection is the source's sweep candidate; sustained directional bodies beyond the boundary favor its breakout interpretation.
3. Separately classify the approach as impulsive or corrective. The speaker expects a forceful approach to be more compatible with continuation and a slower one with a sweep/reversal.
4. Keep those as hypotheses until a complete trigger and risk policy are defined. The source does not quantify strong, immediate, impulsive, slow, or sustained.

## Operational choices still needed

A reproducible version needs swing confirmation, approach window, normalized range/momentum measures, candle-body/wick thresholds, recovery distance, acceptance horizon, entry timing, stop, target, size, and expiry. A label assigned after several later candles cannot justify a fill at the initial crossing. Higher-timeframe context and actual volume are also not fully specified in this clip.

## Failure cases and evaluation

A forceful approach can exhaust at the level; a slow approach can accelerate through it. A rejection can later fail and an accepted break can reverse. Test the approach classification and post-crossing reaction separately against all eligible extremes on later data, include costs, and report conditional outcome frequencies rather than treating the verbal probability claims as calibrated statistics. This partial lesson offers two contextual checks, not a complete three-confirmation trading system.

## Local evidence and reproducibility

Approximately 0–42s discusses reaction candles; 42–83s discusses approach speed. The narration ends after the second topic despite the opening promise of three checks.

# Bearish-to-bullish structural recovery with a breaker/gap overlap and a 2R example

Source: [ChartTactix](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1EAUrwonU2/). Downloaded duration: 126.18 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The source begins with a declining swing sequence, then identifies an impulsive recovery through prior lower highs and evaluates a later pullback into an area marked as a breaker overlapping a fair-value gap. The proposed long follows a rejection there, invalidates beneath the breaker, and targets 2R. The speaker explicitly omits pairs/timeframes because the video is intended to teach concepts rather than copied signals.

## How to reproduce the described logic

1. Mark the earlier lower lows/lower highs using a declared swing rule.
2. Wait for an upward move through the relevant lower-high references and treat it as a possible structural recovery, not certainty that an uninterrupted uptrend follows.
3. Mark the illustrated breaker/gap overlap before the later retest. The clip names these objects but does not fully define their detection algorithm.
4. Wait for price to revisit and reject the area.
5. Evaluate the long with invalidation beneath the breaker and an objective twice the entry-to-stop distance, subject to a declared executable fill model.

## How to make the concept reproducible

Additional choices must define the timeframe, instrument/feed, pivot confirmation, break-close rule, breaker origin, gap formula, overlap tolerance, rejection candle, stop buffer, size, and expiry. The deliberate absence of a pair/timeframe is part of the educational format, but an actual backtest still needs them. A top-down study should use completed higher-timeframe information, not the final state of a bar that had not ended at entry.

## Failure modes and evaluation

Breaking lower highs can lead to a range or another decline; a zone overlap can fail or never retest. The favorable 2R example is not a success-rate estimate. Compare the same recovery-and-retest entry with and without the overlap filter on later data, include unfilled candidates, losses, and costs, and preserve all structural references as known at each step. A later perfect-looking zone should not replace the original one after observing the outcome.

## Local evidence and reproducibility

About 12–55s describes the prior structure and recovery; 61–85s describes overlap, rejection, stop, and 2R; 86–126s explicitly explains why instrument/timeframe are omitted and emphasizes conceptual study.

# A declining-trend pullback into a gap and trendline before an illustrated short continuation

Source: [Crypto Insights](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1FjhXubJms/). Downloaded duration: 22.36 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The animation shows a downtrend, a lower-high reference, a falling line, and a bearish gap left by a decline. Price recovers toward that gap/line area and the image then illustrates another decline with a short-position overlay. The chart uses generic-looking price axes and does not establish an actual market, timeframe, or trade record.

## How to reconstruct the pictured setup

1. Mark the prior lower-high sequence and falling reference line using only available pivots.
2. After the downward expansion, mark the shown bearish gap region.
3. Wait for the later recovery toward that area rather than chasing the earlier decline.
4. Define a bearish rejection/entry condition independently; the animation does not specify the exact candle or order rule.
5. The overlay places invalidation above the local pullback region and a larger objective below. A nominal reward/risk annotation is a plan, not proof of an attainable exit.

## Information still required

Instrument/feed, timeframe, swing algorithm, line tolerance, gap geometry, first-touch rule, rejection trigger, stop buffer, target formula, position size, and expiry are absent. An intrabar excursion around a drawn line need not be the same as a completed structural break. Future swings must not be used to select a cleaner historical line.

## How to evaluate it

As additional research, freeze the trend/line/gap construction and compare a location-only short with a confirmed-rejection short on later data. Include recoveries that resume upward, gaps that never retest, missed fills, costs, and failed targets. The final large decline is selected to illustrate the idea; the title's cleanest-entry claim does not establish that the entry was recognizable at that exact historical price.

## Local evidence and reproducibility

About 3–6s adds the lower high and falling line; 10s marks the gap during recovery; 13–16s adds the short overlay; 19–22s reveals favorable continuation.

Source: [Trade Empire](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1EBHDJgXfy/). Downloaded duration: 383.988 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Trade Empire demonstrates Mirage Liquidity Sweep Pro, credited to Willy Algo Trader. It marks unswept buy-side and sell-side swing liquidity, including equal highs/lows, then scores a wick-through-and-reclaim event. This is an indicator workflow; the full score formula is not disclosed.

## How to reproduce the illustrated method

1. Identify an unswept swing or equal-high/low reference.
2. Require a wick beyond it and a close back across the reference.
3. Apply the minimum score. The score ranges from 0 to 100; volume is described as a 15% component, with penetration depth and reclaim strength together accounting for more than half.
4. With Require CHoCH enabled, wait for a minor structure break within the confirmation window. Turning it off allows the earlier sweep signal and changes the strategy.
5. The script permits one trade at a time and suppresses a bar that sweeps both sides.
6. Place the stop beyond the sweep wick plus a buffer. TP1 is described as just over 1R, TP2 as 2R, and TP3 as 3R. After TP1 is touched, the illustrated stop moves to entry.

## Missing rules and interpretation limits

The visible inputs around 132–143s establish Swing Length 21, Max Sweep Distance 80 bars, Min Sweep Score 60, Require CHoCH enabled, Structure Pivot Length 8, and Confirmation Window 13 bars. The filter panel around 110s shows volume MA length 21, volume spike multiplier 1.5, enabled volume/HTF-bias options, and a four-hour HTF setting. The final choppy-market variant changes the minimum score to 65, leaving CHoCH enabled. These are demonstrated settings, not validated optimal parameters. Stop buffer, target allocations, fees, exact score formula, and fill rules remain unspecified. Higher-timeframe bias nudges the score rather than vetoing all contrary trades. A long can therefore occur with bearish higher-timeframe bias. A stop at entry does not make the position costless or immune to slippage.

## Settings and evaluation distinctions

The suggested higher score in choppy conditions is discretionary tuning, not an independently validated universal optimum. Test the default confirmation and immediate-sweep branches separately. For staged exits, track remaining quantity after each target and whether the stop change becomes active only after a real TP1 fill. # Liquidity-location awareness: obvious extremes, volume nodes, and waiting for a reaction

Source: [Trading experience](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1dD5iht2pW/). Downloaded duration: 236.866 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The source uses a busy-road analogy to argue that price often interacts with conspicuous highs, lows, support/resistance, and high-volume areas. It urges traders to avoid chasing and to consider where clustered stops may sit. It is a discretionary location lesson, not a specified entry system.

## How to reproduce the illustrated method

1. Mark repeated/equal highs and lows and the relevant supply/demand areas before price arrives.
2. If using volume profile, distinguish the point of control and high-volume nodes from swing-price liquidity references. They measure different things.
3. Observe whether price sweeps an obvious extreme and then reclaims it or continues through.
4. Wait for a defined reaction before a new trade. The video does not provide the exact trigger.
5. Additional implementation choice: choose invalidation from a complete setup and adjust size to its stop distance under a fixed risk budget. The source does not provide that sizing rule.

## Missing rules and interpretation limits

The assertion that a stop-out means the analysis was right but the stop was wrong is not established. Moving a stop farther away can increase loss without improving expectancy. No chart alone proves someone intentionally hunted that order. The source leaves zone construction, entry, stop formula, target, timeframe, and size open; promised later lessons are not present in this file.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

The roughly four-minute narration discusses crowded levels, stop placement, profile references, and waiting until after the liquidity interaction.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of the complete machine transcript, saved caption, and timestamped chart evidence.

# A bullish fair-value gap with midpoint holds and an order-block overlap

Source: [Ali Khan](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/19nocASSpF/). Downloaded duration: 123.439 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The lesson combines a bullish three-bar fair-value gap with an overlapping bullish order block. It calls repeated holds around the gap midpoint level 2 bullish FVG, a source-specific label. The midpoint/consequent-encroachment discussion is context; the example later describes an entry at the high of the gap inside the order block.

## How to reproduce the illustrated method

1. Mark the bullish gap between the first candle high and third candle low after the third candle closes.
2. Mark the preceding three down-close candles described as the bullish order block.
3. Check the overlap and observe the source’s repeated midpoint holds, including the absence of closes below the referenced midpoint.
4. For the narrated order variant, use the high/upper edge of the FVG within that overlap, and identify equal highs as the objective.
5. Choose a separate, explicit stop and invalidation before entry; neither is adequately defined in the clip.

## Missing rules and interpretation limits

Do not collapse the midpoint context and the upper-edge limit order into one price. The instrument, timeframe, order expiry, first-touch policy, and risk size remain unspecified. The source’s claim that no buyers/sellers met in the gap is an overstatement: outer-candle gap geometry does not establish an absence of counterparties during the middle candle.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

The 123-second narration covers the gap and midpoint, the preceding down-close candles, overlap entry, and equal-high objective.

# Two separate trades: an order-block short followed by a lower-zone long

Source: [Gowin Trades](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1MZm2X6JwQ/). Downloaded duration: 93.933 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Gowin Trades narrates a bearish order-block rejection and then a reversal trade from a lower swept area. The first setup uses the upper wick/zone as short location; after its profit target, the second uses the lower zone for a long. They are sequential examples, not a rule requiring an immediate flip after every winner.

## How to reproduce the illustrated method

1. Establish the initial downward context and mark the upper order-block/rejection area.
2. In the illustrated short, enter within the rejection wick, place the stop above the block, and assess a 3R target.
3. After that trade completes, separately reassess the lower swept/recovery area.
4. The source takes the illustrated long at that lower zone with a stop beneath it and the previous high as objective.
5. Calculate that second trade’s reward/risk from its actual levels; a prior high is not automatically 3R.

## Missing rules and interpretation limits

The exact block boundaries, close-versus-touch confirmation, timeframe, instrument, stop buffer, size, and reversal eligibility are omitted. The lower-zone long is described more directly than a confirmed structure-entry rule, so adding a confirmation would be a separate research version.

# Four structure-reading lessons: trend, valid pullback, swing legs, and an HTF-aligned shift

Source: [Smart Risk](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1DtZeKrNqQ/). Downloaded duration: 728.109 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Smart Risk develops a hierarchy for distinguishing an ongoing impulse from a real pullback and for using a lower-timeframe structure shift after a higher-timeframe zone is reached. Its key distinction is that candle color alone does not create a valid pullback.

## How to reproduce the illustrated method

1. Establish the higher-level HH/HL or LL/LH sequence and identify the protected recent swing.
2. In a bullish impulse, track the last bullish candle’s low. A later breach of that low establishes the illustrated pullback; a small red candle contained above it may remain part of the impulse. Candle color is not the decisive test. Mirror this for a bearish leg.
3. Separate impulse, corrective, and continuation phases; do not promote every small internal pivot to a major swing.
4. For the short execution example, locate a fresh/unmitigated higher-timeframe supply, FVG, breaker, or mitigation area during a bullish lower-timeframe retracement within a broader bearish context.
5. Require a close below the most recent relevant lower-timeframe pullback low. A wick alone is not the stated MSS confirmation.
6. The proposed sell-limit location is a bearish FVG, order block, or inverse FVG within the shift leg. The objective is nearby current-timeframe liquidity or a relevant higher-timeframe level.

## Missing rules and interpretation limits

Pullback recognition may use a breach/wick, while the later MSS entry requires a close: these are separate tests. The source does not specify a numeric timeframe pair, a complete pivot algorithm, stop formula, size, order expiry, or tie-breaking among overlapping entry areas. Equal highs and internal sweeps need a consistent rule before automation.

## How to study and implement the hierarchy

Replay the examples with future candles hidden. At each bar record the currently protected major swing, the last impulse candle reference, and any internal pullback. Delay a label until the source condition occurs; a visually obvious completed swing can be unknowable at its extreme. Then freeze which internal low is eligible for MSS and which entry area is chosen if several exist. Compare the structural filter and the entry model separately, retaining unfilled limits and failed shifts. A valid structure description supplies context, but the missing risk policy still prevents a complete executable strategy.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

About 40–207s covers trend; 209–400s valid pullbacks; 401–563s impulse/correction/continuation; 572–727s higher-timeframe zones and the execution shift.

Source: [SMC Charts](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1FAzqye3kW/). Downloaded duration: 105.906 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The example warns against confusing a local downward shift after consolidation with the failure of the protected major higher low. The bullish branch requires that lower zone to hold and price to react upward; a close below protected support would change the analysis.

1. Mark the bullish HH/HL expansion, its break of structure, and the protected low.
2. Recognize the later internal bearish displacement as a warning without automatically reclassifying the whole swing.
3. At the lower area, wait for rejection and a confirmed upward shift before the illustrated long.

sources.overview: Tarzan Trading TT combines directional structure and a 200 EMA with MACD crosses. It then adds a 20 EMA close filter after the initial examples. A long cross must occur below MACD’s zero line, while a short cross must occur above it; a cross anywhere on the pane is not enough.
sources.gaps: The narrator incorrectly describes the two plotted MACD curves as the fast 12-period and slow 26-period moving averages themselves. Its claim that the added filter removes 80% of bad trades is not demonstrated.

## Proposed integration

# Candlestick anatomy, momentum, and confirmation at key levels

Source: [Trade DNA](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/18DEMCeztw/). Downloaded duration: 2318.833 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Trade DNA’s long class teaches candles through body size, wicks, location, and higher-timeframe context. Its most concrete execution example waits for a bearish engulfing candle at resistance, then sells with a stop above the level and an objective at the next support. Large portions repeat earlier explanations rather than adding new strategies.

## How to reproduce the illustrated method

1. Read OHLC correctly: on an up candle the body runs from open below to close above; on a down candle it runs from open above to close below. Upper and lower shadows extend to the high and low.
2. Compare body and wick size with neighboring candles. The source interprets expanding bodies and small wicks as stronger directional movement, shrinking bodies as slowing movement, and a long rejection wick as a possible warning.
3. Establish a relevant support/resistance zone or valid trendline before interpreting the candle. Avoid treating every random isolated shape as an entry.
4. Start with higher-timeframe context, with H4/daily mentioned as examples, then inspect a lower chart for the local reaction.
5. At the chosen level, allow breakout, rejection, or sideways movement as possible outcomes. Wait through indecision.
6. In the final short example, a substantial bearish engulfing candle confirms rejection after resistance consolidation. The source enters on that completed signal, places invalidation above resistance, and targets the next key level.

## Missing rules and interpretation limits

No body/wick threshold, support algorithm, fixed timeframe pair, exact engulfing containment rule, stop buffer, size, or expiry is established. Earlier claims that momentum always slows before a reversal, that wickless candles never pulled back, or that body size proves high volume are too strong. OHLC does not reveal the intrabar path, total traded volume, identities, or intentions. A wickless candle means open/close coincide with extremes; price may still have fluctuated between them.

## Pattern categories and practical limits

The three categories named are engulfing patterns (bullish/bearish), star formations (morning/evening), and doji. The lesson names these families but does not fully specify every formation’s geometry or gaps. A tweezer-bottom failure on a lower chart is used to advocate higher-timeframe context, not to prove that all lower-timeframe signals are weaker. Color alone is not the wick interpretation, but it still encodes the relationship between open and close. The final insistence on waiting for confirmation is more restrictive than earlier statements that a long wick itself is confirmation; use one declared entry model rather than selecting whichever looks best afterward.

## A reproducible additional study

Normalize body and wick sizes by recent range or volatility and freeze the threshold before testing. Choose support/resistance from information available before the approach; do not retrospectively draw levels only where price reversed. Test the source’s big-medium-small sequence separately from the final engulfing trigger. Keep trades with a nearby objective that cannot justify the planned risk as rejected candidates. A 1R, 2R, or 3R label alone does not determine expectancy; record frequency, win/loss size, costs, missed entries, and drawdown. The lesson’s risk-management advice is general and does not prescribe a personal risk fraction.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

0–145s introduces shrinking bearish bodies at support; 460–590s anatomy; 635–900s rejection wicks; 925–1183s body strength and wickless candles; 1185–1460s repeats fading momentum/wicks; 1527–1818s location and top-down context; 1825–1960s ratios; 1993–2100s pattern categories; 2116–2274s confirmation and risk.

# BigBeluga consolidation ranges: ADX detection, delta context, and a close outside the box

Source: [Trade Empire](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/18azX612PU/). Downloaded duration: 396.063 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The tutorial demonstrates Consolidation Range [BigBeluga] on five-minute GBP/JPY. Low ADX identifies candidate consolidation, a box tracks its high/low, and up/down volume delta provides directional context. Despite predictive wording, the narrated order waits for a close beyond the range.

## How to reproduce the illustrated method

1. Add the named script and verify its version. The baseline describes ADX threshold 15 for day trading or 25 for swing use and smoothing length 10.
2. Let a range develop for at least 15 bars in the baseline example.
3. Read positive versus negative delta as context, with near-zero delta a reason to wait.
4. Enter only after a candle closes beyond the box in the intended direction.
5. The illustrated long stop lies below the midpoint, and the short stop above it.
6. The objective is 1.5–2 times the range HEIGHT. This is a price-distance multiple of the box, not automatically 1.5–2R.

## Missing rules and interpretation limits

The ADX is a strength measure, not a direct measurement of volatility or institutional accumulation. Delta’s construction and denominator need the actual code/data; a displayed percentage does not prove signed exchange order flow. The source does not fully establish whether bounds freeze, how overlapping ranges reset, or how size and fills are handled. Claims about catching 90% of breakouts are not independently supported.

## Other presets in the narration

Forex: ADX threshold 20, smoothing 12, minimum 18 bars. Crypto: threshold 12, smoothing 8, roughly 12–25 bars, plus a delta-above-60% suggestion whose exact formula is not provided. Stocks: threshold 25, smoothing 15, with a reference to 07:00–09:30 EST premarket. These are alternative suggestions, not one consistent universal setting. Freeze session timezone and daylight-saving handling if testing them.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Keep the baseline and later claims separate and verify the script’s actual input definitions before attempting to reproduce them. The claimed future prediction and institutional-money identification are not validated by the demonstration.

39–120s covers components; 165–217s baseline inputs; 227–295s line entries; 296–349s momentum; 350–411s wave comparisons; 435–532s market presets. Original frames at 167.65, 182.89, 198.13 and 213.37s were inspected for the baseline.

# A five-point falling-wedge/Wolfe-wave-style bullish drawing

Source: [TradersNotes](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1R4iZUaJ2L/). Downloaded duration: 23.266 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The silent animation numbers alternating pivots 1 through 5, highlights a lower entry region, draws an upward objective line through earlier pivots, and reveals a rally. This resembles a bullish Wolfe-wave-style construction, but the clip does not provide a named, complete formal definition.

## How to reproduce the illustrated method

1. Identify the five alternating swing points in the displayed descending structure.
2. Draw the two descending boundary lines and the rising projected objective line used in the example.
3. Mark point 5 near/below the lower boundary as the illustrated entry region.
4. Place the depicted invalidation beneath that region and use the upward projected line as the displayed target reference.
5. Define the actual entry trigger independently: the animation’s Entry label does not say whether to buy a touch, a reclaim, or a later close.

## Missing rules and interpretation limits

Instrument, timeframe, pivot confirmation, required geometry, time symmetry, tolerance, and order execution are absent. The sloping target changes with time, so a test needs its equation and target-update rule. The final selected rally is not proof the five-point pattern will complete on every occurrence. Original samples show the five labels, lower highlighted entry region, target line, stop-loss region, and favorable final expansion.

# Two trendline methods: stochastic-confirmed bounces and structure-confirmed breaks

Source: [TRADING CHART](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/19zDRs1Ced/). Downloaded duration: 889.005 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

This tutorial first treats a trendline as a zone, then gives two distinct strategies. The bounce method combines the zone with a stochastic excursion and return. The reversal method combines a weakening swing sequence with a decisive close beyond the trendline.

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `ac3f33cf8e64b176abe064c2355950bd19b1fee74d46433b3355f5028018e50a`.

Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Build bounce and structural-break branches around frozen trendline anchors. Stochastic is K length 5, K smoothing 3, D smoothing 3; source bands need verification. Chart-fitted maximum-touch lines must be recalculated on prefixes rather than borrowed from future history.

**Indicators:** [analysis/rule_catalog.py](../../analysis/rule_catalog.py) and [analysis/rule_engine.py](../../analysis/rule_engine.py) supply typed indicator operands/comparisons; [analysis/indicator_engine.py](../../analysis/indicator_engine.py) supplies MACD, SMA, Wilder RSI and other series. Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. **Indicators evidence:** Export feature values and each condition’s pass/fail reason. Test exact numeric fixtures, cross equality, recursive seeds and constant-price/zero-variance cases. Compare individual filters before the combined stack.

**Lines evidence:** Show boundary equations and decision-time prices, false breaks, no-retests and invalidations. Test a future extreme that would refit the finished chart: it must leave earlier experiment lines unchanged.

Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

The settings panel at 498s shows stochastic %K Length 5, %K Smoothing 3, and %D Smoothing 3, on the chart timeframe with Wait for timeframe closes checked. The numeric overbought/oversold bands are not shown; do not assume 80/20 as source settings. Touch tolerance, major-pivot algorithm, close distance, stop buffer, timeframe, and size are also open. **Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. # Four gold frameworks: sweeps, RSI divergence, trendline continuation, and trendline reversal

Source: [AM Trader](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/18okxnqn9f/). Downloaded duration: 1118.667 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

AM Trader presents four related gold frameworks, generally executing on five-minute charts with hourly context. They share a wait-for-confirmation approach and an objective at the next meaningful level, requiring at least 2:1 reward/risk. The examples use discretionary structure and zones rather than a full mechanical algorithm.

## How to reproduce the illustrated method

1. Sweep method: mark repeatedly tested support/resistance. At resistance, require a break above and close back below; check hourly bearish context, then use the reclaim candle close for the illustrated short, with the stop above its wick and target at the next level. Mirror the setup at support. The long example says below support for the stop, which still needs a precise boundary.
2. RSI divergence: compare lower PRICE-BODY lows with higher RSI lows for bullish divergence, or higher body highs with lower RSI highs for bearish divergence. Check hourly context and wait for an engulfing/rejection close. The bullish example stops below the engulfing bar and targets next resistance.
3. Enhanced divergence: combine a known level, a sweep/reclaim, and RSI divergence, then verify higher-timeframe context. The short enters on the close back under resistance, stop above the wick, target lower support.
4. Trendline continuation: draw a zone through multiple major touches, wait for an engulfing reclaim or pin-bar rejection, confirm hourly context, then enter on the completed candle with invalidation beyond it.
5. Trendline reversal: require weakening structure or double rejection before a break, then confirm the higher-timeframe picture. The detailed short also uses an hourly broken order block/breaker and bearish engulfing rejection; entry is on the bearish confirmation close, stop beyond its wick, target next support.

## Missing rules and interpretation limits

RSI settings, exact pivot matching, divergence lookback, engulfing geometry, trendline width, buffers, and size are not fully specified. The instruction to use bodies for divergence should not be silently replaced by wick extremes. Higher-timeframe ranging examples are accepted when a relevant range boundary rejects, so the filter is broader than a simple same-direction trend-only rule. Sweeps do not prove deliberate institutional manipulation.

## Timeframe map and research procedure

The final map pairs 5m/15m execution with hourly context, hourly execution with daily, four-hour execution with weekly, and daily execution with monthly. These are alternative workflows. Use only completed higher-timeframe information at a lower-timeframe decision. Evaluate each of the four methods separately before combining them; mixing every discretionary filter makes it impossible to attribute performance. A fixed 2R target and a next-level objective are compatible only when that objective is far enough away under the selected entry and stop.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

24–250s sweeps; 253–492s divergence and the enhanced variant; 496–776s trendline construction/continuation; 779–1028s reversal and the breaker example; 1036–1100s top-down timeframe suggestions.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of the complete machine transcript, saved caption, and timestamped chart evidence.

# Fresh displacement zones and a London-to-New-York sweep framework

Source: [CY FOREX](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1BrjNkrhYv/). Downloaded duration: 1008.708 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

CY FOREX presents two related five-minute methods. The first selects fresh displacement-origin zones and waits for a sweep/reclaim with thirty-minute context. The second references a London-session level that New York later sweeps, again requiring higher-timeframe alignment. Shark terminology is a narrative for the price action, not evidence identifying institutional orders.

## First framework: select the zone before timing entry

1. Identify a fast directional departure with large decisive bodies and limited hesitation.
2. Require that departure to break a prior structural high/low.
3. Mark its origin as the candidate zone and prefer its first return; the source rejects already-used zones.
4. Require a liquidity sweep and closing reclaim at the fresh zone, rather than entering on its initial touch.
5. Check the thirty-minute context before the five-minute entry. In the AUD/CAD example, a higher-timeframe support sweep supports the bullish idea.
6. The illustrated long enters on the confirming close, stops below the zone, and targets the next key level. The zone-evaluation section requires at least 3:1 reward/risk.

## Second framework: session-level reversal

1. Add the Sessions indicator credited to JRFXAddict. Hide the Asian session; set London and New York opacity to 50. These are display settings, not predictive parameters.
2. During London, mark the most recent major support/resistance reference.
3. During New York, wait for price to sweep that reference and close back across it.
4. Before entry, check the thirty-minute chart. The USD/JPY short is rejected because the higher timeframe is breaking upward; the Solana long is accepted with an upward higher-timeframe context.
5. Enter on the five-minute confirming close, place invalidation beyond the referenced level, and target the next opposing level. The Solana example is described as 4R; that is an example, not a mandatory fixed target for every session trade.

## Missing rules and evaluation

Exact session hours/timezone, daylight-saving policy, displacement thresholds, zone boundaries, pivot confirmation, maximum age, stop buffer, size, and order expiry remain open. The second framework is explicitly session-limited; do not apply it all day. A higher-timeframe range can support either direction depending on location, so alignment needs a frozen rule rather than hindsight about intent. Claims that the market rewards shark behavior or that all failed sweeps result from random zones are not demonstrated. Keep the two methods and their minimum-R rules distinct. Record first-return eligibility as it existed at the decision, and use only higher-timeframe candles available at that time.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

118–340s displacement-zone quality and minimum 3R; 345–650s sweep timing and thirty-minute alignment; 665–777s session setup; 778–917s EUR/USD and rejected USD/JPY; 928–989s aligned Solana example.

# NQ stop-distance comparison: fixed eight points versus a buffered structure stop

Source: [Doubaz Capital](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1cSKRPNWNM/). Downloaded duration: 110.92 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Doubaz Capital reviews an archived October 6, 2026 Nasdaq example on a one-minute chart. A short around 31,598 with an eight-point stop is said to be clipped at 11:28 by one tick, while a stop two points above the 11:15 high survives and reaches 2R roughly 41 minutes later. This is a selected retrospective case, not an independently verified live result.

## How to reproduce the illustrated method

1. Before entry, identify the actual structural invalidation and add a declared price buffer.
2. Compare that distance with recent one-minute candle range, described as about 10.5–10.6 points here.
3. Set contract quantity from the chosen distance and a fixed dollar-risk budget, rather than forcing the stop to accommodate a desired contract count.
4. In the source’s $500 example, it contrasts 31 micro contracts at eight points with 12 contracts at the wider structural stop.
5. Keep these as alternative pre-entry plans. The clip does not justify widening an already active losing stop.

## Missing rules and interpretation limits

The side-by-side graphic around 47s shows the fixed stop at 31,606.00 and the structure stop at 31,618.50; the sizing slide explicitly labels the wider distance 20.5 points. Full execution costs and actual fills are not established. The fact that a wider stop wins this selected example does not prove that wider stops improve the strategy over all trades. A stop beyond a high can still fail or slip. The archival price and date are not current guidance.

## Contract arithmetic

The primary [CME Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 specification](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/equities/nasdaq/micro-e-mini-nasdaq-100.contractSpecs.html) gives MNQ a $2 value per index point and a 0.25-point tick worth $0.50. Thus 31 × 8 × $2 = $496 before fees/slippage, leaving only $4 of a $500 budget for all costs. An additional sizing formula is floor(budget / (stop distance × point value + per-contract cost allowance)). Do not apply the micro multiplier to the larger NQ contract. The displayed 20.5-point alternative can be checked: 12 × 20.5 × $2 = $492 before fees/slippage, leaving $8 of the $500 budget. Thus both source sizing examples are arithmetically consistent before costs; neither establishes an executed result.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

The roughly 111-second narration gives the entry, fixed stop, one-tick stop-out, buffered high alternative, later 2R outcome, average candle range, and position-count comparison.

# Dealer gamma as a conditional regime filter for fades versus breakouts

Source: [HataTrades](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1C5SRixbj2/). Downloaded duration: 66.64 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

HataTrades distinguishes long-gamma dealer hedging, which can oppose price moves, from short-gamma hedging, which can reinforce them. The source uses the gamma regime as context for deciding whether to consider fading a zone or joining a breakout; order flow supplies timing and the zone supplies location.

## How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Obtain a timestamped estimate of dealer NET gamma for the relevant underlying and options universe. The clip does not identify a data provider or estimator.
2. Positive estimated dealer gamma suggests that delta rebalancing may buy weakness and sell strength; negative gamma suggests the reverse.
3. Use that regime as context for a separately defined zone and order-flow trigger.
4. Reassess when the estimate changes rather than treating one morning label as permanent.
5. Define risk, exit, and eligibility independently; none is specified in this short lesson.

## Missing rules and limitations

Gamma is not an up/down forecast, and positive gamma does not guarantee pinning or a successful fade. Dealer exposure is an estimate requiring inventory assumptions, expiries, strikes, and a timestamp. The clip supplies no exact setup, stop, target, or tested performance.

## Primary-source clarification

[Research hosted by Cboe](https://cdn.cboe.com/resources/education/research_publications/gammasqueezes.pdf) describes the conditional hedge mechanism: negative-gamma delta hedging can amplify moves and positive gamma can attenuate them. It also emphasizes that the strength depends on exposure magnitude and whether dealers rebalance. This supports a conditional mechanism, not the clip’s certainty about what every day must do.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

The 66-second narration explains positive and negative gamma, then calls location the where, order flow the when, and gamma the why.

# A static guide to bullish breakouts and bearish breakdown retests

Source: [Pips & Profits](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1ExWVocycS/). Downloaded duration: 10.005 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The ten-second image contrasts consolidation beneath resistance with a bullish breakout and later confirmation, and consolidation above support with a bearish breakdown and retest. It teaches the shape of a level break; the saved caption mainly advertises training.

## How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Mark the upper resistance and lower support of the preceding consolidation before the move.
2. For the bullish example, observe price breaking above resistance and later holding near it as support.
3. For the bearish example, observe the break below support and return toward it as resistance.
4. Treat the labeled confirmation/retest as a location concept. The image does not define a specific candle or order.
5. Add a precise close/touch rule, invalidation, target, and sizing policy for any executable version.

## Missing rules and limitations

No timeframe, instrument, minimum range duration, breakout distance, retest tolerance, stop, or target is supplied. Both examples are clean illustrations; false breaks, missed retests, and failed role reversals remain possible. The training/broker links are promotions and add no trading rules to this file.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

All sampled frames show the same How Breakouts Work graphic with resistance, consolidation, breakout, support, breakdown, and retest labels.

Reviewed using: manual inspection of sampled original frames and the saved caption; no speech.

[Downloaded video](video.mp4) · [Page description](video.description) · [Timestamped machine transcript](transcript.txt) · [Sampled frames](frames/contact-sheet.jpg) · [Metadata](video.info.json) · [Integrity record](source.json)

Machine transcripts may misrecognize names, numbers, and music. Settings and claims that could not be established are identified above. Any implementation examples added in this writeup are research choices, not extra rules attributed to the video.

# Integration plan: A static guide to bullish breakouts and bearish breakdown retests

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `19d9c788a2fe36ca4f06702f24863be91ec8d6d28f32ebab22df8dc8b5ec46e8`.

## Experiment overview

The ten-second image contrasts consolidation beneath resistance with a bullish breakout and later confirmation, and consolidation above support with a bearish breakdown and retest. It teaches the shape of a level break; the saved caption mainly advertises training.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Evaluate the particular setup or indicator sequence described here on a frozen historical universe. First produce causal features and candidate events; promote it to a trade simulation only after the unresolved entry, invalidation, exit and sizing decisions below have an explicit versioned specification. A daily-equity adaptation must be labeled when the source uses another interval or product.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Mark the upper resistance and lower support of the preceding consolidation before the move.
2. For the bullish example, observe price breaking above resistance and later holding near it as support.
3. For the bearish example, observe the break below support and return toward it as resistance.
4. Treat the labeled confirmation/retest as a location concept. The image does not define a specific candle or order.
5. Add a precise close/touch rule, invalidation, target, and sizing policy for any executable version.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Create a source-specific adapter for the sequence in the Rules and inputs section, preserving the order in which each illustrated reference and confirmation becomes known. Store candidate, armed, confirmed, expired and invalidated events separately. [patterns/base_pattern.py](../../patterns/base_pattern.py) supplies signal/annotation structures, while [indicators/_signal.py](../../indicators/_signal.py) demonstrates latest-bar output; neither supplies the missing source rules. A recap or undisclosed indicator stays blocked until its actual generator and execution specification are available.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and limitations

No timeframe, instrument, minimum range duration, breakout distance, retest tolerance, stop, or target is supplied. Both examples are clean illustrations; false breaks, missed retests, and failed role reversals remain possible. The training/broker links are promotions and add no trading rules to this file.

**Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

# Williams Vix Fix with stochastic confirmation and an optional order-block filter

Source: [Tarzan Trading TT](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1FLTn3GbhN/). Downloaded duration: 551.693 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Tarzan Trading TT demonstrates CM Williams Vix Fix Finds Market Bottoms by Chris Moody, initially on four-hour Ethereum, using default Vix Fix inputs. A green volatility-extreme flash is a candidate bottom, not an immediate buy. Stochastic confirmation is added to handle repeated flashes and failed first signals.

## How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Add the original Chris Moody bottom-focused script. The narrator prefers H4 or daily and leaves its inputs at default.
2. Add Stochastic. Custom values are referenced but not reliably established in the reviewed source evidence.
3. Require a green Vix Fix flash and the blue stochastic line to reach oversold.
4. Wait for a completed bullish stochastic cross above the orange line, then use the illustrated long. Stop below the recent swing low, target 2R.
5. The optional order-block version adds LuxAlgo Order Blocks Detector and requires the pullback to enter a block before the Vix Fix/stochastic conditions. Its stop is the block MIDLINE, with either 2R or an overhead block as objective.

## Missing rules and limitations

Do not merge the swing-low stop with the optional midpoint stop. Repeated green flashes do not reveal which will precede the final low. One continuation example verbally reverses the line-cross wording, while the main long definition consistently uses blue over orange. Exact oscillator settings, signal coincidence window, stop buffer, size, and script versions remain open.

## Separate top-detection variant

The narrator also names a modified CM Williams Vix Fix Find Market Tops and Bottoms credited to Aaron Stone. In that version the shown colors differ: green marks a candidate top and red a bottom. Its short example requires overbought stochastic followed by blue crossing below orange, a stop above the swing high, and 2R. The author says they prefer the original bottom method. Do not apply the original green-means-bottom rule to the modified color scheme, and do not treat Vix Fix as the exchange VIX itself.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

63–155s original tool/H4/defaults; 165–295s repeated flashes and stochastic; 301–341s continuation; 350–473s tops-and-bottoms variation; 493–550s order-block variant.

Reviewed using: manual reading of the complete timestamped machine transcript and saved source material.

sources.gaps: The example groups bullish EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and DXY as confirmation of USD strength. That is directionally inconsistent: rising EUR/USD and GBP/USD conventionally indicate stronger quote-currency alternatives relative to USD, whereas rising DXY indicates a stronger dollar basket. # Supertrend Confluence Signals: ATR trend, volume filter, and a cross-market table

Source: [Trade Empire](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/19mShrfdre/). Downloaded duration: 353.8 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The tutorial uses Supertrend Confluence Signals [AlgoAlpha] on fifteen-minute EUR/USD. It combines a trend line, volume visualization, retracement markers, and a multi-asset/timeframe table. The source calls it a complete system, but important execution and directional-confluence details are unresolved.

## How to use or reproduce the lesson

# Probability Grid: historical swing distributions, three trading variants, and a probability-reading error

Source: [Trade Empire](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1AA5aPVHso/). Downloaded duration: 360.048 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Trade Empire introduces Probability Grid [LuxAlgo] on fifteen-minute EUR/USD. It projects a ten-by-ten grid from past swing statistics. The narration repeatedly treats extreme-zone numbers as exact reversal odds; that interpretation needs correction before its trade rules can be reproduced.

## How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Baseline: Normalize Data on; swing length 20; maximum reversals 50; Beyond Each Cell mode; show grid and top-right dashboard.
2. Narrated trend-pullback branch: look for an 80–90% area against an established trend, then require rejection/engulfing or volume confirmation; stop beyond the grid boundary and target next resistance/support with about 1.5R.
3. Narrated range branch: first observe 20–30 consolidation bars, then seek an 85%+ extreme with rejection; stop beyond the zone, target opposite boundary, with midpoint partial profits offered.
4. Narrated breakout branch: a strong-volume close past the claimed 95%+ extreme triggers continuation; stop at the prior probability zone and use a range/pattern measured move.
5. Before implementing any branch, resolve how those percentages map to the script’s chosen probability mode.

## Missing rules and limitations

A displayed beyond-cell probability is not the chance of reversing on the next bar and not a win rate. Historical swing sampling, pivot delay, changing distributions, and small samples matter. More reversals do not automatically establish statistical significance. The narration does not fully define rejection candles, volume, measured-move multiplier, size, or how stops map to grid prices.

## Primary-source correction and presets

The [script author’s description](https://www.tradingview.com/script/9royDOd6-Probability-Grid-LuxAlgo/) says Beyond Each Cell displays the estimated mass OUTSIDE the rectangle from the last reversal to the cell. Its 9% example corresponds to 91% within that rectangle, not a 91% immediate reversal or profitable-trade probability. Within Each Cell is a different quantity; default decile cells have approximately 1% each. The video’s threshold language therefore cannot be coded literally without checking the mode. Its alternative swing-length/reversal-count presets are Forex 25/75, crypto 15/40, stocks 30/60, futures 20/50. None is independently validated here.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

32–85s grid modes; 104–153s baseline; 162–288s three trade branches; 312–354s alternative settings.

# Waddah Attar Explosion V2: momentum above an expanding volatility threshold

Source: [Trade Empire](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1EFDCrY9BE/). Downloaded duration: 417.798 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The lesson demonstrates Waddah Attar Explosion V2, credited to SHK, on fifteen-minute EUR/USD. A colored directional momentum histogram is compared with an explosion line and a dead-zone threshold. The actual entry is reactive at the next candle open after the four conditions align.

## How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Baseline settings: sensitivity 120, fast MA 20, slow MA 40, Bollinger channel length 20, standard-deviation multiplier 1.8.
2. Long: green histogram rising, crossing above the explosion line; both histogram and explosion line above the dead zone; explosion line itself rising.
3. Short: red histogram magnitude rising above the explosion line, with the same dead-zone and rising-line conditions. Red bars rising in magnitude are bearish momentum, not a bullish signed-value increase.
4. Enter at the next open after confirmation. The example stop is beyond the recent swing and the target 1.5R.
5. The narration also offers histogram back below explosion as a primary exit, explosion line turning down as a secondary exit, and histogram falling into the dead zone as an emergency exit.

## Missing rules and limitations

The ordering of the 1.5R target and three indicator exits needs a declared policy. Swing lookback, buffers, size, and exact definition of rising are absent. A histogram above twice the explosion value is called especially strong, but no calibrated probability is supplied. Claims of eliminating 70% of losses and automated profits are marketing assertions without a complete audit.

## Narrated alternative presets

Forex: sensitivity 100 and BB multiplier 2.2, favoring London/New York overlap. Crypto: 180/1.5. Gold: 90/2.5. Stocks: sensitivity 120 and BB length 25, avoiding the first thirty minutes after the open. Keep these variants separate from the baseline and test them on later data; the word best does not establish optimization quality.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

19–94s tool/components; 146–188s baseline; 193–282s entries and exits; 291–303s ratio; 331–396s presets.

Reviewed using: manual reading of the complete timestamped machine transcript and saved source material.

[Downloaded video](video.mp4) · [Page description](video.description) · [Timestamped machine transcript](transcript.txt) · [Sampled frames](frames/contact-sheet.jpg) · [Metadata](video.info.json) · [Integrity record](source.json)

Machine transcripts may misrecognize names, numbers, and music. Settings and claims that could not be established are identified above. Any implementation examples added in this writeup are research choices, not extra rules attributed to the video.

# Integration plan: Waddah Attar Explosion V2: momentum above an expanding volatility threshold

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `ac9136208046049c605826cfe7b80091d32e3249504f4ae90f6552bf32c1b192`.
