**Proposed evaluation scope:** Evaluate the particular setup or indicator sequence described here on a frozen historical universe. First produce causal features and candidate events; promote it to a trade simulation only after the unresolved entry, invalidation, exit and sizing decisions below have an explicit versioned specification. A daily-equity adaptation must be labeled when the source uses another interval or product.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Baseline settings: sensitivity 120, fast MA 20, slow MA 40, Bollinger channel length 20, standard-deviation multiplier 1.8.
2. Long: green histogram rising, crossing above the explosion line; both histogram and explosion line above the dead zone; explosion line itself rising.
3. Short: red histogram magnitude rising above the explosion line, with the same dead-zone and rising-line conditions. Red bars rising in magnitude are bearish momentum, not a bullish signed-value increase.
4. Enter at the next open after confirmation. The example stop is beyond the recent swing and the target 1.5R.
5. The narration also offers histogram back below explosion as a primary exit, explosion line turning down as a secondary exit, and histogram falling into the dead zone as an emergency exit.

### Writeup: Narrated alternative presets

Forex: sensitivity 100 and BB multiplier 2.2, favoring London/New York overlap. Crypto: 180/1.5. Gold: 90/2.5. Stocks: sensitivity 120 and BB length 25, avoiding the first thirty minutes after the open. Keep these variants separate from the baseline and test them on later data; the word best does not establish optimization quality.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Add Waddah Attar Explosion series using the stated sensitivity 120, 20/40 MAs, BB length 20 and multiplier 1.8 after formula verification. Resolve precedence between 1.5R and the three indicator exits before composing a trade adapter.

**Indicators:** [analysis/rule_catalog.py](../../analysis/rule_catalog.py) and [analysis/rule_engine.py](../../analysis/rule_engine.py) supply typed indicator operands/comparisons; [analysis/indicator_engine.py](../../analysis/indicator_engine.py) supplies MACD, SMA, Wilder RSI and other series. Match formulas before reuse: rsi() is rolling-mean RSI, rsi_wilder() differs, and atr() uses span EMA rather than Wilder ATR. [indicators/_math.py](../../indicators/_math.py) has Wilder ATR/EMA/DEMA building blocks. Stateful sequences or missing formulas need a dedicated adapter rather than forced Builder conditions.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

**Source interval constraint:** This writeup includes intraday/tick or hourly branches. Select any source-supported daily branch explicitly; the following constraint applies to the finer-interval branches. Daily OHLCV cannot reconstruct its internal ordering, session windows or lower-frame confirmation. The owner has local hourly loaders but the history API has no hourly route, and hourly bars cannot recover one-/five-/fifteen-minute or tick data. A faithful branch remains blocked until a suitable historical source and remote access contract exist. Any added daily-bar equity adaptation needs a separate identity and explicit changed rules; do not present it as the original experiment.

Warm slowMA40, its momentum calculation and BB20, including all required shifted comparisons and variance initialization.

Use the longest selected rolling/recursive dependency plus prior-value comparisons and confirmation delay. Treat indicator NaNs as not-ready; never backfill initial values from later bars. Keep each market/interval series independent.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

**Indicators evidence:** Export feature values and each condition’s pass/fail reason. Test exact numeric fixtures, cross equality, recursive seeds and constant-price/zero-variance cases. Compare individual filters before the combined stack.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and limitations

The ordering of the 1.5R target and three indicator exits needs a declared policy. Swing lookback, buffers, size, and exact definition of rising are absent. A histogram above twice the explosion value is called especially strong, but no calibrated probability is supplied. Claims of eliminating 70% of losses and automated profits are marketing assertions without a complete audit.

**Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

The final checklist unexpectedly says Funded Algo aligned timeframes, although that is not one of the five tools just taught. No exact combined time window, stop, target, size, tightening formula, or full QQE/MACD inputs is supplied. Trend-age percentiles are not guaranteed reversal probabilities, zero lag is not foreknowledge, and candle-color delta does not prove institutional trades. # Linear Regression Candles plus UT Bot: a downtrend-filtered short recipe

Source: [TRADING CHART](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/18kuguxpaK/). Downloaded duration: 27.585 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The reel combines Linear Regression Candles with UT Bot Alerts and says to restrict shorts to a downtrend. It supplies more input detail than exit detail, and one ATR value differs between spoken instruction and the visible input field.

## How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Add Linear Regression Candles. Set signal smoothing to 7; the inspected frame also shows Simple MA enabled, Lin Reg enabled, and regression length 11.
2. Add UT Bot Alerts. Key value is 2. The narration says ATR period 1, while inspected settings frames around 15.7–17s show 11 selected in the field. Record this conflict and verify the intended final value before implementing.
3. The Signals from Heikin Ashi Candles option is unchecked in the shown settings.
4. Use a sell signal only with a separately defined downward market context.
5. The narration puts the short stop at the recent swing high; it does not give a full target or sizing rule.

## Missing rules and limitations

Do not borrow the later thirty-minute Heikin-Ashi recipe from another reel without labeling it a separate variant. This clip does not fix timeframe, instrument, trend algorithm, whether a regression-candle close is required, entry timing, stop buffer, or exit. # Wait for the higher-timeframe long location before searching for a lower-timeframe trigger

Source: [notbradgohadvice](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1EAeuBQkGg/). Downloaded duration: 24.31 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The speaker says price is too early/far from a chosen lower long area and advocates waiting until it reaches that location, then dropping to a lower chart for entry criteria. They also describe a possible short through the interim pullback.

## How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Mark the intended higher-level long area before price approaches.
2. Do not declare a long merely because the broader idea is bullish when the source’s location condition has not occurred.
3. At that area, switch to the lower chart and evaluate an explicit entry model. The clip does not teach that model.
4. Treat a short through the pullback as a separate setup requiring its own conditions and risk. Waiting is also a valid decision; the absence of a long does not logically require a short.

The location’s construction, timeframe pair, lower-timeframe confirmation, invalidation, target, and size are absent. The narration’s statement that one must short current action if longs are not eligible is an overreach. Opposite-direction trading is not automatically justified by a preferred long zone being lower.

The 24-second narration contrasts the current price with the lower entry area and mentions switching charts only after arrival.

# A self-revising trading-agent loop advertisement and its evaluation problem

Source: [Raycfu](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1FEjc1YaBA/). Downloaded duration: 47.181 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Raycfu describes a proposed system that translates an idea into code, tests five years of history, uses a critic to rewrite losing entry/exit logic, retests, and saves failed versions. It then advertises automatic live deployment with fixed risk limits. No working code, dataset, or reproducible results are shown.

## How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Specify a strategy and preserve the original implementation/version.
2. Evaluate it on a declared training period and record errors and trade outcomes.
3. Let proposed revisions form new versions rather than overwriting the evidence.
4. Use independent validation periods and a final untouched holdout; repeatedly optimizing on the same losses is not new evidence.
5. Test execution and risk controls outside the model’s editable strategy logic before considering any deployment. These validation steps are additional implementation guidance, not demonstrated product behavior.

## Missing rules and limitations

The claims of a five-year stress test in seconds, never repeating a mistake, and risk limits an agent can never override are not established by the reel. 0–18s idea/code/backtest; 19–38s critic/rewrite/deploy/history loop; 40–47s promised external guide.

# Volumatic VIDYA: cloud pullback with signed candle-volume delta

Source: [Trade Empire](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/19Fr2extYi/). Downloaded duration: 424.389 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Trade Empire demonstrates the BigBeluga Volumatic Variable Index/VIDYA tool on fifteen-minute GBP/JPY. A cloud supplies direction, while delta compares volume assigned to bullish versus bearish candles. The final template waits for a pullback to the cloud rather than buying its color change immediately.

## How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Add the specific BigBeluga script and record its version.
2. Long template: green cloud, delta above +30%, then price returns to test the cloud. The stop is below the recent low and the target 2R.
3. Short template: red cloud, delta below −30%, then a bounce into the cloud; stop beyond the recent high and target 2R.

The source’s 65,000 versus 49,000 example produces about 28.1% if divided by their average, close to its 27.9% claim; dividing by their sum gives about 14.0%. # Rolling Z-Score Trend: mean reversion, divergence, and trend qualification

Source: [Trade Empire](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1NmDLGezkV/). Downloaded duration: 369.058 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The lesson uses Rolling Z-Score Trend [QuantAlgo] on four-hour EUR/USD. It standardizes the current close against a rolling mean and standard deviation, then uses momentum columns. Its mean-reversion, divergence, and trend-following applications are separate hypotheses and should not be mixed after an outcome is known.

## How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Baseline: lookback 50, EMA smoothing 3, information table and momentum columns enabled.
2. Mean-reversion short: Z above +2 and red/decelerating momentum columns. Long: Z below −2 and green/improving momentum. The source proposes a stop at ±2.5 and first objective at zero.
3. Divergence: compare price highs with Z-score peaks, and price lows with Z-score troughs, using weakening momentum columns as context. The source mistakenly calls lower price lows/higher Z lows bearish; that geometry is conventionally bullish divergence.
4. Trend qualification: sustained Z above +1 with green momentum is the bullish example. A separate confluence suggestion compares 1h and 4h extremes.
5. Convert any Z-based exit into a declared dynamic signal/price execution policy; a Z coordinate is not a fixed market stop price.

## Missing rules and limitations

A rolling-price Z-score above two standard deviations does not itself prove a less-than-5% event frequency or a high reversal probability. Such probability statements require distributional assumptions and empirical calibration. The lookback mean/deviation changes each bar, so a Z-level stop can move even if price does not. No complete divergence pivot rule, trend exit, position size, or order policy is supplied.

## Formula and alternative presets

The primary [QuantAlgo script description](https://www.tradingview.com/script/rbeErVR5-Rolling-Z-Score-Trend-QuantAlgo/) gives Z=(close−rolling mean)/rolling standard deviation, followed by 3-period EMA smoothing and bar-confirmed signals. Its standardized score is not a calibrated future probability. The video’s suggested alternatives are Forex lookback 60/smoothing 3/extremes ±1.8, crypto 30/±2.5, gold 40/±2, and SPY/QQQ 50/±1.6. These are source suggestions without an independently audited optimization.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

28–122s tool/settings; 146–199s mean reversion; 204–241s divergence; 245–281s trend and MTF; 304–365s presets.

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `29ced458f963ac5762a5e2291693faddb94519692b54f653364a348b45076227`.

## Experiment overview

Tristan Ford’s silent animation labels a combination of trendline liquidity sweep, FVG, and Fibonacci. It contrasts an early local setup with a broader descending-line/channel context, then illustrates a long after a lower sweep and retracement into a small gap/discount area.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Evaluate the particular setup or indicator sequence described here on a frozen historical universe. First produce causal features and candidate events; promote it to a trade simulation only after the unresolved entry, invalidation, exit and sizing decisions below have an explicit versioned specification. A daily-equity adaptation must be labeled when the source uses another interval or product.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to use or reproduce the lesson

1. Mark the broad descending references and the smaller local line separately.
2. Observe the local break and later sweep below the nearby low rather than assuming the initial breakout completes the trade.
3. Mark the bullish recovery leg and its displayed FVG/retracement area.
4. The final drawing locates a long near that lower area, risk beneath the local low, and an objective at the upper descending reference.
5. The original 19.27s frame labels the lower retracement line 0.786 inside the FVG region. Specify the exact Fibonacci anchors, gap boundaries, and confirmation before implementing; the drawing alone does not establish whether a touch of 0.786 is a mandatory entry trigger.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

**Lines:** [analysis/trendlines.py](../../analysis/trendlines.py) is a useful geometry/display reference, but its fitted anchors and tolerances need evaluation on each available prefix. Freeze the writeup’s wick/body boundaries and trigger sequence before reuse.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Load the full permitted formation/anchor window and confirmation bars before eligibility. Store line slope/intercept, tolerance and any later replacement as a new version; daily-to-intraday conversion cannot recover missing anchors.

Retain the zone-formation/impulse history before the chosen date range. A three-candle gap becomes known only after its third candle; a block validated by later displacement becomes available only after that validation. Missing formation history makes it unavailable.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

**Lines evidence:** Show boundary equations and decision-time prices, false breaks, no-retests and invalidations. Test a future extreme that would refit the finished chart: it must leave earlier experiment lines unchanged.

**Zones and gaps evidence:** Export original zone bounds, formation/availability, every return and invalidation. Test early touches before zone availability, overlapping zones, no-return moves and failed retests. Do not treat institutional-order narratives as OHLCV-observed facts.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and limitations

No instrument, timeframe, price scale, fully specified retracement/entry rule, stop buffer, position size, or expiry is disclosed. The final check mark is a selected outcome. A sweep and attractive Fibonacci alignment do not establish a complete order rule or make the later upper-line touch inevitable.

**Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. **Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. 1. Identify the rounded lower-high sequence and its common support area before the break.

The short thanks in the transcript adds no operational instruction.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Original samples show the curved decline into support, the printed pattern reference, and the later downside expansion.

# Four-hour structure and imbalance with a 75% retracement limit

Source: [Simple Markets](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/17z6yS1mEg/). Downloaded duration: 57.949 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Simple Markets describes a swing method using the four-hour trend, a clear bullish structure break, remaining imbalance, and a deep Fibonacci retracement. The displayed template is entry 75, stop 100, target zero, with orientation chosen so the long stop is at the swing low and target at the swing high.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Establish the H4 trend.
2. Require a clear break of structure in that direction.
3. Identify the imbalance left by the impulse.
4. Wait for retracement rather than chasing the expansion.
5. Anchor the Fibonacci to the impulse extremes, checking the actual prices: in the bullish template 100% is the low/invalidation and 0% the high/objective.
6. The proposed limit is the 75% retracement, with stop at the low and objective at the high. Ignoring costs and buffers, reward is 75% of the range against 25% risk, or 3R.
7. The caption suggests infrequent review rather than managing every five-minute fluctuation.

## Missing rules and limitations

Trend/pivot confirmation, minimum imbalance, exact swing anchors, order expiry, partial fills, cost allowance, size, and weekend/overnight policy remain open. The selected winner and claimed payouts are not independently verified. A default drawing-tool orientation may reverse 0 and 100, so verify the economic levels rather than copying the drag direction blindly.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

0–26s trend/BOS/imbalance; 26–48s retracement and Fibonacci; 48–58s selected result and CTA. The on-screen checklist confirms entry 75/SL100/TP0.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of the complete machine transcript and saved source material.

# Waiting until after a stop run: a liquidity-timing maxim

Source: [Stoicadx Connected Page](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1KRSdpX78r/). Downloaded duration: 32.483 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The source argues that good entries often occur after crowded traders have been stopped and that discomfort can accompany those entries. It provides an intuition about waiting, not a precise liquidity or order-flow measurement.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Identify the obvious prior extreme before it is crossed.
2. Observe the actual sweep and subsequent behavior.
3. Require a separately declared reclaim or structure confirmation rather than treating discomfort as a signal.
4. Set risk and target independently.
5. Record sweeps that continue in the original direction as well as those that reverse. These steps turn the intuition into a research question; the video does not supply the definitions.

## Missing rules and limitations

No timeframe, instrument, entry, stop, target, size, or proof of stop inventory is given. The claims that the best trade is always hard and that institutions engineer every sea of liquidity are overgeneralized. Feeling reluctant to buy does not itself establish an edge.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

The full thirty-two-second speech discusses entries after stop-outs and the psychological difficulty of taking them.

# Thirty-minute consolidation volume profile and a POC continuation pullback

2. Draw a fixed-range volume profile across it.

No profile row resolution, feed, range algorithm, higher-timeframe pair, general stop/target formula, or complete sample is supplied. POC is not itself an unfilled-order ledger. The closing 90% gold-signal claim concerns an advertised community and is not validated by these examples.

0–27s repeats the range/profile/breakout/POC sequence; 30–40s adds higher-timeframe bias and the signal-service invitation.

# Trendline bounce and reversal tutorial: a repost with the same two core methods

Source: [Cryptology](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1FQHTLNwzH/). Downloaded duration: 920.425 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

This tutorial first treats a trendline as a zone, then gives two distinct strategies. The bounce method combines the zone with a stochastic excursion and return. The reversal method combines a weakening swing sequence with a decisive close beyond the trendline.

## How to reproduce the illustrated method

1. Identify at least two obvious major swing points and connect lows in an uptrend or highs in a downtrend. The source chooses wick/body placement that captures more touches and allows a zone rather than a perfect line.
2. Bounce long: price approaches rising support, the blue stochastic line enters oversold, then crosses back out into the normal band. Enter the illustrated long, stop slightly below the local swing low, target 2R.
3. Bounce short: price approaches falling resistance, the line enters overbought and then crosses back down into the band. Stop above the local swing high, target 2R. A support-to-resistance overlap is an example of extra confluence.
4. Breakout long: an established downtrend stops making lower lows and forms a higher low, then price closes clearly above the descending trendline zone. Stop slightly below the break area and target 2R.
5. Breakout short: higher highs give way to a lower high, followed by a clear close below rising support. Stop above the break area and target 2R.

## Missing rules and interpretation limits

The settings panel at 498s shows stochastic %K Length 5, %K Smoothing 3, and %D Smoothing 3, on the chart timeframe with Wait for timeframe closes checked. The numeric overbought/oversold bands are not shown; do not assume 80/20 as source settings. Touch tolerance, major-pivot algorithm, close distance, stop buffer, timeframe, and size are also open. A diagonal-line break alone does not prove a trend reversal.

## How to make the discretionary drawing testable

Record the anchors and zone width before the next encounter; do not refit the line after a failed trade. A maximum-touch choice over an entire completed chart can introduce hindsight. Declare how many prior bars are eligible and when a swing is confirmed. Keep the bounce and break methods separate, including their different stops. The stochastic trigger is a crossing back out of an extreme zone, not merely a %K/%D crossover anywhere in the pane.

## Relationship to the other archived source

This repost repeats the same trendline/stochastic tutorial body as item 120 and adds a longer final guide invitation. Both clips show stochastic 5/3/3 in the 498s settings frame. Numeric extreme bands are not established, and the body/wick maximum-touch rule needs a causal anchor policy. No external guide was followed.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

61–214s uses; 227–395s drawing; 458–657s stochastic bounce methods; 671–885s weakening structure plus a decisive breakout close; 889–920s external guide/community invitation. The tutorial body matches item 120, but this URL and local media remain independently archived.

# Integration plan: Trendline bounce and reversal tutorial: a repost with the same two core methods

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `a9d137ad04dc0f1538e7a0ddc5e67e236aa4f97b906330380b68e99bee127664`.

## Experiment overview

This tutorial first treats a trendline as a zone, then gives two distinct strategies. The bounce method combines the zone with a stochastic excursion and return. The reversal method combines a weakening swing sequence with a decisive close beyond the trendline.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Evaluate the particular setup or indicator sequence described here on a frozen historical universe. First produce causal features and candidate events; promote it to a trade simulation only after the unresolved entry, invalidation, exit and sizing decisions below have an explicit versioned specification. A daily-equity adaptation must be labeled when the source uses another interval or product.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to reproduce the illustrated method

1. Identify at least two obvious major swing points and connect lows in an uptrend or highs in a downtrend. The source chooses wick/body placement that captures more touches and allows a zone rather than a perfect line.
2. Bounce long: price approaches rising support, the blue stochastic line enters oversold, then crosses back out into the normal band. Enter the illustrated long, stop slightly below the local swing low, target 2R.
3. Bounce short: price approaches falling resistance, the line enters overbought and then crosses back down into the band. Stop above the local swing high, target 2R. A support-to-resistance overlap is an example of extra confluence.
4. Breakout long: an established downtrend stops making lower lows and forms a higher low, then price closes clearly above the descending trendline zone. Stop slightly below the break area and target 2R.
5. Breakout short: higher highs give way to a lower high, followed by a clear close below rising support. Stop above the break area and target 2R.

### Writeup: How to make the discretionary drawing testable

Record the anchors and zone width before the next encounter; do not refit the line after a failed trade. A maximum-touch choice over an entire completed chart can introduce hindsight. Declare how many prior bars are eligible and when a swing is confirmed. Keep the bounce and break methods separate, including their different stops. The stochastic trigger is a crossing back out of an extreme zone, not merely a %K/%D crossover anywhere in the pane.

### Writeup: Relationship to the other archived source

This repost repeats the same trendline/stochastic tutorial body as item 120 and adds a longer final guide invitation. Both clips show stochastic 5/3/3 in the 498s settings frame. Numeric extreme bands are not established, and the body/wick maximum-touch rule needs a causal anchor policy. No external guide was followed.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

This repost repeats item 120’s trendline/stochastic methods. Link the experiments as shared-method variants rather than count them as independent validation evidence; preserve this source’s identity and any presentation differences.

**Lines:** [analysis/trendlines.py](../../analysis/trendlines.py) is a useful geometry/display reference, but its fitted anchors and tolerances need evaluation on each available prefix. Use frozen anchor/confirmation records for experiment decisions; do not feed an entire finished chart’s preferred line into an earlier signal.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Load the full permitted formation/anchor window and confirmation bars before eligibility. Store line slope/intercept, tolerance and any later replacement as a new version; daily-to-intraday conversion cannot recover missing anchors.

**Lines evidence:** Show boundary equations and decision-time prices, false breaks, no-retests and invalidations. Test a future extreme that would refit the finished chart: it must leave earlier experiment lines unchanged.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

### Writeup: Missing rules and interpretation limits

The settings panel at 498s shows stochastic %K Length 5, %K Smoothing 3, and %D Smoothing 3, on the chart timeframe with Wait for timeframe closes checked. The numeric overbought/oversold bands are not shown; do not assume 80/20 as source settings. Touch tolerance, major-pivot algorithm, close distance, stop buffer, timeframe, and size are also open. A diagonal-line break alone does not prove a trend reversal.

Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. # Exhaustion Mean Theory: five-minute wick failure back toward VWAP

Source: [G Street Trades](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1EdK8JfiAu/). Downloaded duration: 78.181 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

G Street Trades combines VWAP and a 9 EMA on five-minute charts. After price stretches away from both, it waits for a pronounced exhaustion wick and a break of that candle in the reversal direction, targeting a return to VWAP.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Add VWAP and a 9-period EMA; choose and record the VWAP session/anchor.
2. Wait for price to be stretched away from both references.
3. After an upward stretch, identify the candle that wicks upward and stalls.
4. Sell only when the NEXT candle breaks that exhaustion candle’s low, rather than entering on the exhaustion candle itself. Stop above its wick and target VWAP.
5. After a downward stretch, mirror the method: break of exhaustion-candle high for a long, stop below its lower wick, target VWAP.

## Missing rules and limitations

Stretch distance, wick/body threshold, stall definition, stop buffer, instrument, session, size, and handling of an unbroken next candle are not specified. VWAP evolves during the session, so decide whether the target is fixed at entry or updated. Claims of sixty prop evaluations and payouts are not independently audited.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

6–15s tools/timeframe; 18–40s precise break timing and risk; 46–66s selected examples; 67–78s performance/CTA.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of the complete machine transcript and saved source material.

# Congressional-disclosure copy trading: a data-source idea with material reporting lag

Source: [Myinvestingclub](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1AGRqb6xTz/). Downloaded duration: 32.083 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Myinvestingclub advertises websites such as QuiverQuant and Capitol Trades for following reported congressional transactions. It claims an unnamed bot returned 46% while the S&P 500 returned 12%, and lists five large technology companies. No date range, bot definition, or independently auditable return series is supplied.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Identify an original filing, the traded security, transaction date, reported amount range, and public disclosure date.
2. Distinguish that historical transaction from the first time a copying trader could know it.
3. Freeze a copy policy: eligible filers/assets, execution delay, weighting, holding period, and treatment of amendments.
4. Test purchases only after public availability, using actual later prices and costs.
5. Compare with a declared same-period benchmark, dividends, exposure, and drawdown. These are additional research steps, not a strategy specified in the reel.

## Missing rules and limitations

The legal disclosure regime does not mean every transaction is public immediately or that exact position size/cost basis is known. The bot and top-five-stock claims are undated and unverified. A list of prominent names does not establish causation, privileged knowledge, or a copyable edge.

## Primary-source timing correction

The [House Ethics transaction-report guidance](https://ethics.house.gov/periodic-transaction-report-calculator/) describes covered transactions above $1,000 and the earlier of thirty days after awareness or forty-five days after the transaction. A backtest using the transaction date instead of the later public filing date would give the follower information they did not have.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

The thirty-two-second reel names the sites, gives the 46%/12% claim, and lists Alphabet, Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, and Apple.

# Anatomy of a bearish reversal: close through the higher low, then a failed retest

Source: [RdY Investments](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1HV1e6KQMd/). Downloaded duration: 342.705 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

RdY Investments describes a bullish staircase that loses momentum, breaks its prior higher low with an impulsive downward close, and then retests the broken area as resistance. The short is at the rejection of the retest, not at an arbitrary guessed top.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Establish the prior HH/HL sequence and identify the relevant higher low.
2. Observe fading upward progress and an aggressive bearish leg as context.
3. Require a candle BODY CLOSE below the higher-low reference; a wick alone does not satisfy the stated break.
4. Wait for a pullback to that broken support.
5. Require a clear rejection showing failed recovery of the level, then take the illustrated short.
6. The source puts the stop just above the retest area and treats recovery above it as invalidation. It does not define an exact target.

## Missing rules and limitations

No instrument, timeframe, pivot algorithm, rejection geometry, buffer, target formula, or size is supplied. Statements that buyers are trapped and smart money is taking profit are plausible narratives, not observed inventory data. A close below structure can fail, and a retest is not guaranteed to occur.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

28–79s prior trend; 87–177s momentum and break; 200–214s close-versus-wick rule; 221–283s retest/rejection entry and stop.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of the complete machine transcript and saved source material.

# Supply and demand origins validated by displacement and structure, then confirmed on return

Source: [Tarzan Trading TT](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1kv9AcKJZf/). Downloaded duration: 635.415 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Tarzan Trading TT draws zones from the last opposite-color candle before displacement, requires that departure to break structure, and waits for price to return with confirmation. It distinguishes supply/demand origin areas from levels marked merely because price touched them repeatedly.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Supply: find an aggressive bearish departure that breaks the previous relevant higher low. Mark the high/low of the last bullish candle before it and extend the area forward.
2. Demand: find an aggressive bullish departure breaking the previous swing high. Mark the last bearish candle’s high/low.
3. Favor clean displacement and limited prior retests; do not label every small rejection a zone.
4. Check higher-timeframe context.
5. On return, require an explicit entry model such as a rejection wick, engulfing candle, sweep, or lower-timeframe structure shift. The source lists alternatives rather than one mandatory combination.
6. Supply invalidation is above the zone, demand below. Objectives include previous extremes, an opposing imbalance, or a selected 3R–5R plan.

## Missing rules and limitations

The source initially says full high/low but also allows wick-to-body variants; choose one boundary model before testing. Displacement, freshness, maximum retests, timeframe pair, stop buffer, size, and choice among confirmation types remain open. A structure break and FVG cannot prove who placed orders or that unfilled institutional orders remain there.

## Approach and imbalance filters

The final section prefers a gradual return into demand over an aggressive collapse and favors an FVG left by the original departure. Departure speed and return speed are different observations. One later sentence about slow movement without imbalance is ambiguous; do not convert it into a claim that a slow return is always bad after the earlier explicit preference. Freeze the departure-quality and return-quality rules separately. Claims that first/second tests always exhaust institutions are hypotheses rather than verified inventory facts.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

59–154s definitions/mistakes; 167–330s supply; 345–408s new-zone example; 416–520s demand; 528–632s approach speed, FVG quality, and lower-timeframe confirmation.

Source: [Araf Traders](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1Da5dqmb54/). Downloaded duration: 10.667 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The silent clip marks a bullish CHoCH from a prior decline, a rising support line, and a Side ways zone above the recovered level. It then adds a long-position drawing as price breaks upward from the local consolidation.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Mark the prior downward sequence and the bullish break of its local structural reference.
2. Draw rising support from the recovery lows before the next breakout.
3. Mark the small consolidation above the CHoCH area.
4. Observe the illustrated upward departure. The long rectangle places risk below the local support/box region and reward above.
5. Specify exact breakout close, stop boundary, objective, and size before reproducing it.

## Missing rules and limitations

The clip provides no reliable instrument, timeframe, price levels, pivot delay, line tolerance, target multiple, or execution history. CHoCH and rising support are chart descriptions; they do not prove the final breakout was predictable or that the displayed fill was obtainable.

Original sampled frames show CHoCH, Side ways zone, rising line, and a favorable long rectangle.

# Bullish BOS plus demand/trendline intersection with an upper-liquidity target

Source: [Bwenaro](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/19pQN3Lj8d/). Downloaded duration: 20.27 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

Bwenaro combines bullish structure, a lower demand zone, and rising support. The caption explicitly calls for entry where the demand zone intersects the trendline, a stop below demand, and a target at upper buy-side liquidity, illustrated as 3R.

1. Identify the initial bullish BOS and the major upper highs used as the objective.
2. Mark the demand origin beneath the expansion.
3. Draw the ascending support line from prior valid anchors.
4. Wait for price to return to the demand/trendline intersection.
5. The caption’s entry is at that confluence, stop below demand, target upper liquidity/resistance. Check that the actual geometry offers the stated 3:1 reward/risk; do not force it by moving the stop.
6. If requiring a rejection or lower-timeframe shift, label that as an added confirmation variant rather than a source rule.

Demand and trendline may reflect overlapping price information rather than independent confirmations. # Fast MACD, five-minute RSI, and a Parabolic SAR long recipe

Source: [TRADING CHART](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1F6TJYy9MF/). Downloaded duration: 43.7 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The reel combines a shortened MACD, RSI above 50, and a Parabolic SAR flip beneath price. It claims 210% in a week but supplies neither a complete account record nor a defined risk budget.

## How to reproduce the illustrated idea

1. MACD settings visible in the original panel: fast 5, slow 8, signal smoothing 9, Close source, EMA oscillator and signal averages.
2. Add RSI; the narration asks for a five-minute timeframe. The sampled panel shows RSI length 14 and Chart before that timeframe edit, so distinguish the requested final interval from the intermediate screen.
3. Parabolic SAR: Start .01, Increment .02, Max .2 as shown.
4. Long when the blue SAR dots/line flip below price and RSI is above 50.
5. The narration says exit when MACD is near −0.1. That absolute level needs the actual instrument/units and a tolerance; it cannot be generalized unchanged across assets.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

No initial stop, position size, complete short mirror, or exact execution/exit tolerance is supplied. A profitable-looking rectangle is not a general target rule. MACD is in price-related units, so −0.1 means different things on different instruments. The performance headline is not independently verified.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

9–25s configures the tools; 28–36s gives SAR/RSI long and MACD exit. Original MACD and SAR input frames were inspected.

Reviewed using: manual reading of the complete short transcript and caption, with original chart evidence.

# Bearish Adam-and-Eve top with a neckline break

Source: [Zenix Arixon](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1Hqw6NBE5c/). Downloaded duration: 10.496 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The animation compares a sharp first peak and a broader rounded second peak with an Adam-and-Eve bearish reference. It draws a common neckline, illustrates a downside break, and projects a lower measured objective.

## How to reproduce the illustrated idea

1. Identify the sharper Adam peak and rounded Eve peak in the same upper region.
2. Mark the intervening support/neckline before the break.
3. Wait for the illustrated downside departure; choose a completed-close or retest policy separately.
4. The drawing uses the pattern’s vertical height to frame a lower objective.
5. Define the stop beyond the chosen invalidation and size from that distance; no exact stop is taught.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

Instrument, timeframe, peak-shape tolerance, neckline construction, target-measurement anchors, buffer, and sizing are absent. A rounded second peak alone is not confirmation, and a break can reclaim. The favorable animation is not an audited sample.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Original sampled frames show Bear Adam and Eve, both peak shapes, neckline, entry marking and lower height projection.

Reviewed using: manual inspection of original sampled frames, recognized chart text, and saved caption; no useful spoken rule set.

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `ff9bf0fb100260271f34a1a6a67150ecc57352ad48c559275a1928d6a69be3d6`.

## Experiment overview

Rajlav Finance warns that a break of equal highs/lows may be a trap if price quickly reverses and leaves a long wick. The caption and narration both advise waiting for confirmation rather than immediately trading the breakout.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Start with a causal annotation or filter event study of the described condition. Measure all qualifying cases and compare a separately frozen entry model with and without that condition. A descriptive label or selected reference picture is not automatically an order.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to reproduce the illustrated idea

1. Identify equal highs/lows with a declared tolerance.
2. Observe a later breach.
3. Check whether price reverses back through the reference and leaves the illustrated rejection wick.
4. Wait for an independently defined confirmation before entry. The source does not provide its exact geometry.
5. Set invalidation, target and size separately.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Create a source-specific adapter for the sequence in the Rules and inputs section, preserving the order in which each illustrated reference and confirmation becomes known. Store candidate, armed, confirmed, expired and invalidated events separately. [patterns/base_pattern.py](../../patterns/base_pattern.py) supplies signal/annotation structures, while [indicators/_signal.py](../../indicators/_signal.py) demonstrates latest-bar output; neither supplies the missing source rules. A recap or undisclosed indicator stays blocked until its actual generator and execution specification are available.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. ## Gaps and assumptions

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. # Bullish cup-and-handle breakout with a cup-height objective

Source: [Trader Dhana](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1DUULBMN5u/). Downloaded duration: 19.39 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

Trader Dhana draws a rounded cup, an upper resistance/rim, a smaller handle, and a bullish breakout. A 100%-height projection frames the upper target and the animation reveals a favorable rise.
