Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `e8eace59e4baa29fceaadce693ccd1e1a59265859b609dae1ea6775e7edb74a8`.

## Experiment overview

The static image pairs a schematic with a price chart. Both show an initial rise, a local bearish structure change, a downward break, and a return to an upper area before continuation. A short-position rectangle frames risk above and reward below.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Evaluate the particular setup or indicator sequence described here on a frozen historical universe. First produce causal features and candidate events; promote it to a trade simulation only after the unresolved entry, invalidation, exit and sizing decisions below have an explicit versioned specification. A daily-equity adaptation must be labeled when the source uses another interval or product.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to reproduce the illustrated idea

1. Mark the prior upper swing and the bearish structure break shown in the schematic.
2. Identify the upper zone associated with the new bearish departure.
3. Wait for the illustrated return rather than selling every downward candle.
4. The short drawing uses the zone as location and the lower prior range/extreme as objective.
5. Choose a precise confirmation and risk calculation before reproducing the image.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Create a source-specific adapter for the sequence in the Rules and inputs section, preserving the order in which each illustrated reference and confirmation becomes known. Store candidate, armed, confirmed, expired and invalidated events separately. [patterns/base_pattern.py](../../patterns/base_pattern.py) supplies signal/annotation structures, while [indicators/_signal.py](../../indicators/_signal.py) demonstrates latest-bar output; neither supplies the missing source rules. A recap or undisclosed indicator stays blocked until its actual generator and execution specification are available.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and evidence limits

The silent image supplies no verified instrument, timeframe, prices, zone-generation rule, close/touch entry, stop buffer, position size or result ledger. VIP text and target emojis are promotional rather than evidence. The chart is selected to resemble the schematic.

**Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

# A head-and-shoulders breakdown failure and subsequent bullish reclaim

Source: [The Alpha Trader](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/18qKteiH98/). Downloaded duration: 22.7 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The Alpha Trader contrasts a novice head-and-shoulders short with an operator-psychology interpretation. The selected breakdown reaches a lower area, then reverses and reclaims the neckline/rising support, producing an illustrated long.

## How to reproduce the illustrated idea

1. Mark the left shoulder, head, right shoulder and neckline.
2. Treat the initial breakdown short as a separate strategy branch with its own risk and target.
3. Observe whether price follows through or reclaims the broken region.
4. The later drawing buys the reclaim/recovery with risk beneath the failed-break area and an upper objective.
5. Define the exact reclaim close, local shift and target before testing; operator buy text alone is not an executable signal.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

No timeframe, instrument, neckline tolerance, order timing, stop buffer, size, or complete sample is given. The failed pattern does not prove an operator deliberately trapped participants. The title labels do not establish that all breakdowns should be faded.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Original samples show shoulders/head, Breakdown & sell, the lower target, Operator buy, reclaim, and the selected later rally.

Reviewed using: manual inspection of original sampled frames, recognized chart text, and saved caption; no useful spoken rule set.

Machine transcripts may misrecognize names, numbers, and music. Settings and claims that could not be established are identified above. Any implementation examples added in this writeup are research choices, not extra rules attributed to the video.

# Ascending-triangle close breakout with a last-higher-low stop

Source: [Traderdost](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1KW3ZxC8RE/). Downloaded duration: 24.917 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Traderdost gives a relatively explicit ascending-triangle recipe: flat resistance and rising higher lows, enter only after a close above resistance, stop below the last higher low, and project triangle height upward.

## How to reproduce the illustrated idea

1. Mark the flat upper resistance from prior reactions.
2. Verify a sequence of rising lows beneath it.
3. Wait for a completed candle CLOSE above resistance; do not buy early inside the triangle.
4. Model the entry only after that close is known.
5. Put the example stop below the last confirmed higher low.
6. Measure the triangle’s vertical height and project it upward from the breakout level for the objective.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

Instrument, timeframe, pivot delay, equal-high tolerance, minimum touches, height anchors, stop buffer and size remain unspecified. The target-hit reveal is a selected example. False breaks and orders that fill worse than the signal close must be included in any test.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

0–8s quiz/identification; 8–19s close trigger, stop and measured objective; 20–25s selected result.

Reviewed using: manual reading of the complete short transcript and caption, with original chart evidence.

Twin Tulips’ silent slides describe a five-stage bearish method: liquidity sweep, market structure shift, Fibonacci retracement, overlapping order block, and a limit order. Unlike its generic seven-figure caption, the slides provide a specific .71 entry reference.

## How to reproduce the illustrated idea

1. Identify the upper liquidity sweep.
2. Require the subsequent bearish market-structure shift.
3. Draw the Fibonacci on the bearish leg using the high/low shown by the example.
4. Require an order-block overlap with the .71 retracement level.
5. Place the illustrated sell limit at .71, stop at the leg high, and take-profit at the leg low. Check the drawing orientation so .71 is a retracement toward the high.
6. Decide a buffer and cost policy before sizing; an exact high stop has no automatic allowance for spread or slippage.

No timeframe, instrument, pivot delay, sweep definition, exact MSS close requirement, order-block boundaries, maximum wait, or size is disclosed. A limit can remain unfilled or fill before invalidation. The caption’s earnings claim is not verified by the selected chart.

6.81s liquidity sweep; 10.22s MSS; 13.63s Fibonacci; 17.04s OB matching .71; 20.44s entry .71/SL high/TP low. Original slides were inspected.

# A symmetrical-triangle quiz with conditional upside and downside branches

Source: [Mrr Daady](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/19vUM2dekU/). Downloaded duration: 10.16 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The static quiz asks buy or sell inside converging resistance and support. Its printed answer is conditional: buy if price breaks above the triangle, sell if it breaks below. It does not claim that the current unfinished pattern has a knowable direction.

## How to reproduce the illustrated idea

1. Mark the descending upper resistance and ascending lower support.
2. While price remains inside, keep both illustrated branches open.
3. For the upper break, define a completed-close or retest rule before considering the buy.
4. For the lower break, define the corresponding bearish trigger before considering the sell.
5. Add invalidation, target, size and handling of a whipsaw that breaks both sides.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

No timeframe, instrument, breakout tolerance, close requirement, stop, target, or size is established by the quiz. The arrows show alternative paths rather than completed trades. Choosing a direction from a static image is not equivalent to following a tested strategy.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

All sampled original frames show the same Only Pro Traders quiz and its conditional BUY above/SELL below text.

Reviewed using: manual inspection of original sampled frames, recognized chart text, and saved caption; no useful spoken rule set.

# Bullish CHoCH, FVG, and successive Fibonacci refinements

Source: [Nikhil Khareta](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1Crhx5gi3i/). Downloaded duration: 20.767 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Nikhil Khareta rapidly combines a bullish change of character, fair-value gap, golden-zone measurement, later BOS, and another entry/target measurement. A rising support line and final long rectangle accompany the favorable example.

## How to reproduce or study it

1. Mark the bullish CHoCH and the FVG left by the recovery.
2. Measure the first impulse and identify the displayed golden-zone/FVG overlap.
3. Observe the later bullish BOS rather than treating the initial gap as the final entry by itself.
4. Apply the later Fibonacci to the newer leg and mark its candidate entry region.
5. The final drawing uses that lower region for a long, a stop beneath it, and an upper projected target.
6. Preserve each pair of anchors and the order in which the refinements became available.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The narration names several Fibonacci applications but does not reliably establish every anchor, exact entry ratio, extension target or stop. Visible .786/.382 labels are intermediate references, not necessarily the executed prices. Instrument, timeframe, order trigger, size and expiry are absent. Multiple redraws can create hindsight unless frozen in sequence.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

The 21-second narration names CHoCH/FVG/golden zone/BOS/entry/target; original samples show the two lower regions, rising line and final long.

# Central-pivot entry with adjacent pivot levels as risk references

Source: [TRADING CHART](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1Ez2mmWd2V/). Downloaded duration: 25.966 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The reel uses Pivot Points Standard and recolors the central pivot and first support/resistance levels. It illustrates a trade from the central blue line with an adjacent line as the stop reference; it does not define the directional selection rule.

## How to reproduce or study it

1. Add Pivot Points Standard and identify P, S1 and R1 by label rather than color alone.
2. Reproduce the displayed three-level view and record pivot formula/anchor settings.
3. The final short drawing begins around the central pivot, puts risk at the upper adjacent reference, and reward toward the lower one.
4. Declare the missing bearish/bullish context and confirmation before choosing direction.
5. Define a touch/close entry, buffer, target priority and size separately.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

Changing line colors does not create an edge. The claimed 4% usage statistic is unsupported. The panel shows Number of Pivots Back 15 and Use Daily-based Values checked. Formula type, pivot interval, exact session handling, chart timeframe and trigger are not adequately established. A central-pivot touch alone cannot decide whether to buy or sell.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

8–15s tool/style; 17–26s support/resistance and central-line entry/other-line stop; original samples show the short rectangle.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of the complete transcript, saved caption, and original chart evidence.

[Downloaded video](video.mp4) · [Page description](video.description) · [Timestamped machine transcript](transcript.txt) · [Sampled frames](frames/contact-sheet.jpg) · [Metadata](video.info.json) · [Integrity record](source.json)

Machine transcripts may misrecognize names, numbers, and music. Settings and claims that could not be established are identified above. Any implementation examples added in this writeup are research choices, not extra rules attributed to the video.

# Integration plan: Central-pivot entry with adjacent pivot levels as risk references

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `d8d80b86110901c7114997d2a800ab7a1feb3d931e199a2ad94f55a7376115e6`.

## Experiment overview

The reel uses Pivot Points Standard and recolors the central pivot and first support/resistance levels. It illustrates a trade from the central blue line with an adjacent line as the stop reference; it does not define the directional selection rule.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Evaluate the particular setup or indicator sequence described here on a frozen historical universe. First produce causal features and candidate events; promote it to a trade simulation only after the unresolved entry, invalidation, exit and sizing decisions below have an explicit versioned specification. A daily-equity adaptation must be labeled when the source uses another interval or product.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to reproduce or study it

1. Add Pivot Points Standard and identify P, S1 and R1 by label rather than color alone.
2. Reproduce the displayed three-level view and record pivot formula/anchor settings.
3. The final short drawing begins around the central pivot, puts risk at the upper adjacent reference, and reward toward the lower one.
4. Declare the missing bearish/bullish context and confirmation before choosing direction.
5. Define a touch/close entry, buffer, target priority and size separately.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

indicators/_math.floor_pivots supplies traditional P/S1/R1 from a completed reference OHLC period, but the source’s pivot formula/anchor are not fixed. Compare that baseline explicitly and preserve short entry near P, stop near R1 and objective near S1 as a diagram rather than a completed trigger rule.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and evidence limits

Changing line colors does not create an edge. The claimed 4% usage statistic is unsupported. The panel shows Number of Pivots Back 15 and Use Daily-based Values checked. Formula type, pivot interval, exact session handling, chart timeframe and trigger are not adequately established. A central-pivot touch alone cannot decide whether to buy or sell.

**Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

The short lesson identifies a sharp decline followed by a small upward-sloping corrective channel, then illustrates a short at the flag’s lower break. The final chart extends the profit region well below the flag.

## How to reproduce or study it

1. Mark the initial bearish impulse and subsequent corrective flag boundaries.
2. Wait for the illustrated lower-boundary break rather than shorting solely because a flag is forming.
3. The drawing puts risk above the upper flag/swing region.
4. Declare the lower objective from a fixed measurement or structural level before entry.
5. Keep the actual source wording and drawing separate: the narration says target where the pole starts, which is ambiguous for a bearish setup, while its position drawing is below the flag.

## Local evidence and reproducibility

4–15s defines the flag and expected direction; 15–23s places the short and describes the target; original frames show upper risk and lower reward.

1. Add the exact UT Bot Alerts script.
2. Change the chart candles to Heikin-Ashi.
3. Set ATR period 52 and key value 4 as shown and spoken. The internal Heikin-Ashi source checkbox is a separate option and appears unchecked in the shown panel.

Heikin-Ashi values are synthetic, so fills must be evaluated on actual tradable prices. The cartoon anecdote and above-90% claim are promotional. No chart timeframe, cost model, outcome horizon or exit rule establishes a profitable strategy. Wider/slower settings can reduce frequency without improving net expectancy.

8–19s gives script/chart/input setup; 19–25s asserts sparse reliable signals; original settings frames confirm 4/52.

# Rotating four smaller prop accounts: payout accounting is different from net trading profit

Source: [Chart Fanatics](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1CnLS8iC11/). Downloaded duration: 69.867 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Chart Fanatics presents a drawdown-spread idea: compare one $200,000 account with FOUR $50,000 accounts, trade one smaller account per week, and risk 1% of the active account. The machine transcript’s 450k is a misrecognition; the original board shows four 50K accounts.

## How to reproduce or study it

1. In the hypothetical, allocate week-one through week-four trades to different accounts instead of one shared high-water-mark account.
2. Preserve each account’s equity, drawdown and payout eligibility separately.
3. The board’s weekly percentage outcomes are −7%, +3%, −4%, +4%.
4. On four separate $50k bases, that is −$3,500, +$1,500, −$2,000, +$2,000: aggregate trading P&L −$2,000 before fees.
5. Positive accounts total $3,500 gross. The stated $2,800 payout would correspond to an implied 80% share, if the applicable account terms actually allow it. That payout is not the same as aggregate net profit.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

Risking 1% of $50k is $500, while 1% of $200k is $2,000; the comparison changes dollar exposure as well as account segmentation. Losing accounts, replacement/evaluation costs, payout rules, high-water marks and correlated future losses cannot be omitted. The source’s simple −4% month comparison does not supply a complete equal-exposure compounded study.

Use the same trade stream and equal aggregate risk, then apply each actual account agreement’s drawdown, payout and fee rules. Account rotation can change the timing/eligibility of withdrawals, but does not manufacture a positive expectancy from a losing strategy. This note explains the hypothetical arithmetic; it does not recommend a firm or assert current contractual rules.

# Integration plan: An apparent inverse head-and-shoulders breakout that becomes a bull trap

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `d33b07ad1fbc561f10eeaf807b074588122e8f8c06b0358abdb57a1cd85efb15`.

## Experiment overview

ChartPulsePro illustrates an apparent inverse head-and-shoulders recovery, an attempted neckline break, a quick failure, and a later bearish continuation. A lower region is labeled Entry Candle in the selected example.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Evaluate the particular setup or indicator sequence described here on a frozen historical universe. First produce causal features and candidate events; promote it to a trade simulation only after the unresolved entry, invalidation, exit and sizing decisions below have an explicit versioned specification. A daily-equity adaptation must be labeled when the source uses another interval or product.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to reproduce or study it

1. Mark the apparent neckline and recovery structure before the break.
2. Observe whether price accepts above it or returns below.
3. The illustrated case fails/rejects above the neckline, then breaks lower.
4. Treat the later bearish candle as a new candidate requiring its own rule, rather than selling merely because the pattern resembles a trap.
5. Define invalidation, target and size independently.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

**Head and shoulders:** Review [patterns/008_head_and_shoulders.py](../../patterns/008_head_and_shoulders.py) and the corresponding v2 modules as separate baselines. [patterns_v2/patterns/common.py](../../patterns_v2/patterns/common.py) disables head_shoulders/inv_head_shoulders in normal v2 discovery; a future experiment must explicitly select a reviewed adapter rather than assume they are enabled.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Retain the prior trend, all confirmed peaks/troughs and the neckline as known before the break; a later right shoulder cannot justify an earlier entry.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

**Head and shoulders evidence:** Validate chronological shoulder naming, neckline break and failed/reclaimed cases, including any source label conflicts.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and evidence limits

No timeframe, instrument, neckline tolerance, close requirement, stop, target or sample-wide evidence is supplied. The graphic’s inverse-H&S cross and bull-trap check describe the selected outcome; they do not reveal its probability in advance.

**Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

Source: [Flux Charts](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1FoaM4Rexq/). Downloaded duration: 47.808 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Flux Charts uses three tools on a five-minute example: Support and Resistance Logistic Regression, Time Relative Volume Oscillator, and Fibonacci Golden Wave. The long combines a support retest, low selling pressure, and a return to the wave.

## How to reproduce or study it

1. Add the three specifically named Flux Charts scripts and preserve their versions/inputs.
2. Identify support from the logistic-regression overlay and wait for the retest R label.
3. Check the relative-volume oscillator for the described low selling pressure.
4. Wait for price to retest the Fibonacci Golden Wave.
5. Take the illustrated long, place the stop below the most recent low, and target 2R.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

Exact model inputs, probability calibration, low-pressure threshold, wave settings, simultaneous-condition window, stop buffer and size are not supplied. ## Data handling

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. For the initial incomplete-specification state, report the missing dependencies and any captured configuration/signal evidence; trading metrics remain unavailable. Product slogans, floating P&L, dashboards and selected chart rectangles are not validated performance.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Exact model inputs, probability calibration, low-pressure threshold, wave settings, simultaneous-condition window, stop buffer and size are not supplied. A model’s support-holding percentage is not automatically the trade’s win probability. An R label may arrive after the touch, so establish availability before modeling a fill.

# An interview trailer about process, statistics, relative strength, and persistence

Source: [Words of Rizdom](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1AMoQxBYZf/). Downloaded duration: 102.4 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Words of Rizdom introduces Clement and promotes an interview using large competition-return claims. The substantive themes are treating trading as a business, knowing one’s statistics, tolerating failed A-plus setups, and studying stocks that hold up while the broad market falls.

## How to reproduce or study it

1. Keep a complete trade record, including failed valid setups.
2. Review setup frequency, realized wins/losses, costs and drawdown rather than simply aiming to trade less.
3. For the relative-strength idea, compare a stock with a declared benchmark over the same interval and identify those holding steady/rising while the benchmark falls.
4. Use a separate entry and risk model before trading that observation.
5. Study the full process before treating a trailer as a method. These are additional research applications of its themes.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

No full setup, timeframe, entry, stop, target or size is provided. Relative strength does not prove institutions are piling in; other flows can produce it. The 522% and over-1,000% return statements lack the full dates, costs, leverage and record within this clip and are not independently verified here.

0–40s process and competition introduction; 42–69s failed setups/relative strength; 70–102s interview/persistence themes.

# An archived Nasdaq/Asia-session long-management recording

Source: [Adam Trades](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/18faQYv6Po/). Downloaded duration: 25.285 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Adam Trades labels the post a slow Asia session. The chart recording shows a lower-zone long/recovery, upside sell-limit/target-style controls, stop/position adjustments and changing unrealized P&L. It is a trade-management recap rather than a full explanation of how the setup was selected.

## How to reproduce or study it

1. Preserve the historical chart/feed and session. A visible timestamp is September 30, 2026, with UTC−4/ETH on the chart, so do not treat the scene as current Nasdaq guidance.
2. Identify the lower reaction region and long entry shown before the recovery.
3. Track actual order quantities, protective levels and partial exits separately from analysis rectangles.
4. The upper sell-limit controls are consistent with reducing/exiting a long, not automatically a new independent short.
5. Reconcile fills and final closed P&L before claiming the displayed unrealized gains were realized.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The exact instrument contract, setup logic, timeframe hierarchy, initial stop rule, sizing budget and complete account ledger are not established. Dollar figures change as size and price change. The accelerated screen sequence cannot by itself verify net results or a repeatable Asia-session edge.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Original samples across 0–25s show lower entry/recovery, upper sell-limit controls, changing position/P&L, and the September 30 historical timestamp.

Reviewed using: manual inspection of original sampled frames, recognized chart text and saved caption; music is not treated as instruction.

[Downloaded video](video.mp4) · [Page description](video.description) · [Timestamped machine transcript](transcript.txt) · [Sampled frames](frames/contact-sheet.jpg) · [Metadata](video.info.json) · [Integrity record](source.json)

Machine transcripts may misrecognize names, numbers, and music. Settings and claims that could not be established are identified above. Any implementation examples added in this writeup are research choices, not extra rules attributed to the video.

# Integration plan: An archived Nasdaq/Asia-session long-management recording

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `61ca9d33cc8c229dd69e6049e2707708d799f495ded588ce52a4650958256145`.

## Experiment overview

Adam Trades labels the post a slow Asia session. The chart recording shows a lower-zone long/recovery, upside sell-limit/target-style controls, stop/position adjustments and changing unrealized P&L. It is a trade-management recap rather than a full explanation of how the setup was selected.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Evaluate the particular setup or indicator sequence described here on a frozen historical universe. First produce causal features and candidate events; promote it to a trade simulation only after the unresolved entry, invalidation, exit and sizing decisions below have an explicit versioned specification. A daily-equity adaptation must be labeled when the source uses another interval or product.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to reproduce or study it

1. Preserve the historical chart/feed and session. A visible timestamp is September 30, 2026, with UTC−4/ETH on the chart, so do not treat the scene as current Nasdaq guidance.
2. Identify the lower reaction region and long entry shown before the recovery.
3. Track actual order quantities, protective levels and partial exits separately from analysis rectangles.
4. The upper sell-limit controls are consistent with reducing/exiting a long, not automatically a new independent short.
5. Reconcile fills and final closed P&L before claiming the displayed unrealized gains were realized.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Create a source-specific adapter for the sequence in the Rules and inputs section, preserving the order in which each illustrated reference and confirmation becomes known. Store candidate, armed, confirmed, expired and invalidated events separately. [patterns/base_pattern.py](../../patterns/base_pattern.py) supplies signal/annotation structures, while [indicators/_signal.py](../../indicators/_signal.py) demonstrates latest-bar output; neither supplies the missing source rules. A recap or undisclosed indicator stays blocked until its actual generator and execution specification are available.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and evidence limits

The exact instrument contract, setup logic, timeframe hierarchy, initial stop rule, sizing budget and complete account ledger are not established. Dollar figures change as size and price change. The accelerated screen sequence cannot by itself verify net results or a repeatable Asia-session edge.

**Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

# ORB Algo: opening-range break followed by a retest signal

## What it does

Flux Charts explains ORB Algo as an opening-range breakout tool that delays its signal until a retest. It uses the first fifteen or thirty minutes to define the session high/low, rather than a fixed arbitrary chart rectangle.

## How to use or reproduce the source

1. Select the intended session/open and choose a 15- or 30-minute opening window.
2. After that window completes, freeze its high and low.
3. Observe a break above for a bullish candidate or below for bearish.
4. Wait for price to pull back to retest the broken boundary; the script is said to print its signal only then.
5. Add ORB Algo by Flux Charts and verify its exact retest/confirmation inputs and signal availability.
6. Supply stop, target, size and session cutoff independently; the clip does not fully specify them.

# Two Supertrends on five-minute charts: 21/1 and 14/2 agreement

Source: [TRADING CHART](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/19rCd4ZwXL/). Downloaded duration: 47.067 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The reel adds two copies of the Supertrend script credited to Kivanc Ozbilgic. It seeks agreement between different ATR period/multiplier settings and uses a later sell signal as the narrated long exit.

## How to use or reproduce the source

1. Add two copies of the exact Supertrend script.
2. The spoken final settings are ATR period 21/multiplier 1 for the first and period 14/multiplier 2 for the second. Intermediate settings frames show multiplier 3 before those edits; do not mistake the intermediate value for the requested final input.
3. Set the chart to five minutes. The visible Supertrend input panel also uses hl2 source, Chart timeframe, and checks Change ATR Calculation Method, Show Buy/Sell Signals, and Highlighter; these options are part of reproducing the shown variant.
4. Require both Supertrends to give a bullish signal/direction for the illustrated long.
5. Place the stop at the recent support reference and exit on the described Supertrend sell signal.

## Missing rules and limitations

The allowed delay between the two signals, whether both must freshly cross, which copy controls exit, support construction, buffer and size are not specified. Two Supertrends share price/ATR information, so their agreement is not independent evidence. No full performance record is supplied.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

4–25s script/two input sets; 26–36s five-minute agreement; 41–47s support stop and sell-signal exit.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of complete machine transcript, caption and original chart evidence.

# DTC Indicator on USDCAD four-hour charts: multiple selected signals

Source: [dtcindicator3.2](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1EYZwPH2M7/). Downloaded duration: 12.102 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The caption and monitor label identify DTC Indicator on USDCAD H4. The montage shows an extended bullish leg, a later bearish signal/decline, another recovery and a multi-row dashboard. It is a tool advertisement.

## How to use or reproduce the source

1. Identify the exact DTC version and inputs.
2. Save every signal and associated risk/target level at its first availability.
3. Match the USDCAD H4 feed/session if reproducing the example.
4. Define how repeated signals, reversals, open positions and stops are handled.
5. Evaluate all eligible signals with spread, overnight costs and actual fills.

## Missing rules and limitations

No algorithm, full settings, stop/exit policy, size or complete result ledger is provided. Multiple attractive opportunities on one completed chart do not establish a net edge. Patience and discipline are process themes, not substitute risk rules.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Original chart labels and full caption specify USDCAD4H/DTC; samples show bullish/bearish regions and dashboard.

Reviewed using: manual inspection of original sampled frames, recognized chart text and saved caption; music is not treated as instruction.

[Downloaded video](video.mp4) · [Page description](video.description) · [Timestamped machine transcript](transcript.txt) · [Sampled frames](frames/contact-sheet.jpg) · [Metadata](video.info.json) · [Integrity record](source.json)

Machine transcripts may misrecognize names, numbers, and music. Settings and claims that could not be established are identified above. Any implementation examples added in this writeup are research choices, not extra rules attributed to the video.
