# Integration plan: DTC Indicator on USDCAD four-hour charts: multiple selected signals

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `c7c748530c5420b94d0d616164181043292c6035af9129bc9f41436703b0eab2`.

## Experiment overview

The caption and monitor label identify DTC Indicator on USDCAD H4. The montage shows an extended bullish leg, a later bearish signal/decline, another recovery and a multi-row dashboard. It is a tool advertisement.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Start with a specification/prospective-signal capture study. The shown tool, selected recap or undisclosed model does not yet define a reproducible trading engine. Obtain its exact revision, inputs and as-issued signals before enabling a faithful performance run; a public-formula proxy must have a separate experiment identity.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to use or reproduce the source

1. Identify the exact DTC version and inputs.
2. Save every signal and associated risk/target level at its first availability.
3. Match the USDCAD H4 feed/session if reproducing the example.
4. Define how repeated signals, reversals, open positions and stops are handled.
5. Evaluate all eligible signals with spread, overnight costs and actual fills.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Create a source-specific adapter for the sequence in the Rules and inputs section, preserving the order in which each illustrated reference and confirmation becomes known. Store candidate, armed, confirmed, expired and invalidated events separately. [patterns/base_pattern.py](../../patterns/base_pattern.py) supplies signal/annotation structures, while [indicators/_signal.py](../../indicators/_signal.py) demonstrates latest-bar output; neither supplies the missing source rules. A recap or undisclosed indicator stays blocked until its actual generator and execution specification are available.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

**Source interval constraint:** This writeup includes intraday/tick or hourly branches. Select any source-supported daily branch explicitly; the following constraint applies to the finer-interval branches. Daily OHLCV cannot reconstruct its internal ordering, session windows or lower-frame confirmation. The owner has local hourly loaders but the history API has no hourly route, and hourly bars cannot recover one-/five-/fifteen-minute or tick data. A faithful branch remains blocked until a suitable historical source and remote access contract exist. Any added daily-bar equity adaptation needs a separate identity and explicit changed rules; do not present it as the original experiment.

**Instrument constraint:** The source example’s non-equity instrument/feed or contract is not automatically in the US/PH stock-history universe. Check actual symbol/market coverage and preserve price units, sessions and any contract multiplier. An equity/ETF proxy is an additional research hypothesis, not an equivalent dataset.

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

For the initial incomplete-specification state, report the missing dependencies and any captured configuration/signal evidence; trading metrics remain unavailable. Product slogans, floating P&L, dashboards and selected chart rectangles are not validated performance.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and limitations

No algorithm, full settings, stop/exit policy, size or complete result ledger is provided. Multiple attractive opportunities on one completed chart do not establish a net edge. Patience and discipline are process themes, not substitute risk rules.

**Practical next step:** Obtain the exact script/model revision, complete inputs/formulas or lawful timestamped as-issued signals, and its entry/exit/size contract. Capture changing-bar and repaint behavior prospectively. Until then, keep the faithful performance run disabled; use an explicitly named proxy only after specifying its differences.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

# One-hour directional context with a five-minute false-breakout short

Source: [Expertsbazaar Webinar](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1Cvqr2r5gn/). Downloaded duration: 113.172 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Expertsbazaar explains top-down timeframe pairing. Its detailed example gets bearish direction from an hourly liquidity sweep/rejection, then seeks a five-minute bull trap and bearish rejection for execution. The caption also suggests H4 context with fifteen-minute entry as another pairing.

## How to use or reproduce the source

1. Select the pairing in advance: H1→5m for the example, or H4→15m as the caption alternative. The video pairing table also lists D→H1 and M15→M1.
2. On the higher chart, identify the sweep and bearish reaction.
3. Move to the lower chart only after that context is available.
4. Wait for a false bullish breakout followed by a strong bearish rejection in the same area/direction.
5. Plan the short after confirmation; define exact entry, invalidation, target and size separately.

The example short rectangle puts risk above the local bearish rejection cluster, but no general stop/buffer or objective formula is explained. The source also does not mechanically define sweep, rejection, trend bias or close requirement. Higher-timeframe candles still forming cannot be treated as finalized. The complete Hindi narration and caption describe hourly sweep, five-minute bull trap/rejection, pairing alternatives and the webinar invitation.

# Value-area reentry reversals and breakout-hold-structure continuation: a partial tutorial

Source: [FiboGhost X RNS](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1FYMPbd7gp/). Downloaded duration: 484.507 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The file starts mid-lesson, already discussing a return inside value. It fully describes reversal and breakout variants and later mentions a POC-bounce method, but that first method and the initial profile setup are not contained in this downloaded excerpt.

## How to use or reproduce the source

1. Reversal branch: the PREVIOUS SESSION ended inside its value area; in the current session price crosses outside a boundary, then a candle CLOSES back inside. A wick alone is insufficient.
2. The illustrated lower reentry is long with stop near the swing low and 2R target; upper reentry is the bearish mirror with stop near the high and 2R. More candidates may be sought until the session ends.
3. Breakout branch: previous-session closing location may be inside OR outside. Require a significant current-session break, a pullback holding near the broken boundary without deep return into value, and a new structural break in breakout direction.
4. The bullish example requires a new high after the hold; bearish requires a new low. Stop is described as just beyond the break area, target 2R.
5. A failed reversal can be followed by a separately qualified breakout trade; the narrated −1R then +2R equals +1R before costs.

## Missing rules and limitations

Value-area percentage, profile rows/feed, session timezone, initial setup, significance/depth thresholds, swing algorithm, exact stop boundary, size and trade cap remain open. The narration’s generic BOS definition is imprecise, so use its actual higher-high/lower-low examples. A retrospective recovery sequence does not mean every losing reversal has a winning opposite trade.

## Keep the available lesson complete without inventing the missing part

The later claim of three combined strategies is not evidence that this file teaches all three. The POC-bounce algorithm and original configuration are explicitly unavailable here. The two available branches still need a precedence/re-entry policy to avoid hindsight: record when a reversal became eligible, when it failed, and only then when a fresh breakout state satisfied its own conditions.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

0–78s reentry rules; 85–293s breakout/hold/BOS; 305–390s losing reversal plus winning continuation; 410–484s references missing POC/setup material and advertises a blueprint.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of complete machine transcript, caption and original chart evidence.

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `486739efa5fe370cc0c929e9d905dc4493260d8781545c461bee670ebd6b3ebc`.

## Experiment overview

The file starts mid-lesson, already discussing a return inside value. It fully describes reversal and breakout variants and later mentions a POC-bounce method, but that first method and the initial profile setup are not contained in this downloaded excerpt.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Evaluate the particular setup or indicator sequence described here on a frozen historical universe. First produce causal features and candidate events; promote it to a trade simulation only after the unresolved entry, invalidation, exit and sizing decisions below have an explicit versioned specification. A daily-equity adaptation must be labeled when the source uses another interval or product.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to use or reproduce the source

1. Reversal branch: the PREVIOUS SESSION ended inside its value area; in the current session price crosses outside a boundary, then a candle CLOSES back inside. A wick alone is insufficient.
2. The illustrated lower reentry is long with stop near the swing low and 2R target; upper reentry is the bearish mirror with stop near the high and 2R. More candidates may be sought until the session ends.
3. Breakout branch: previous-session closing location may be inside OR outside. Require a significant current-session break, a pullback holding near the broken boundary without deep return into value, and a new structural break in breakout direction.
4. The bullish example requires a new high after the hold; bearish requires a new low. Stop is described as just beyond the break area, target 2R.
5. A failed reversal can be followed by a separately qualified breakout trade; the narrated −1R then +2R equals +1R before costs.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Keep prior-session-inside-value/current-session-reentry reversal and breakout-hold-structure continuation separate. The advertised third POC-bounce method is absent; do not synthesize it from other profile lessons.

**Volume-by-price:** Add a separately sourced volume-by-price/profile adapter only when this source actually requires it: freeze range/session, bin size, value-area algorithm and ties. [analysis/price_volume.py](../../analysis/price_volume.py) computes RVOL/OBV, not POC/VAH/VAL, footprints or resting order inventory. Daily OHLCV cannot identify exact volume traded at each price; a typical-price allocation proxy must be labeled and evaluated separately.

**Swings:** [patterns_v2/patterns/common.py](../../patterns_v2/patterns/common.py) exposes causal ZigZag pivots with separate pivot and confirmation indices; [core/rsi_divergence.py](../../core/rsi_divergence.py) demonstrates evidence carrying pivot/confirmation dates. Reuse these timing ideas only after matching the writeup’s own swing hierarchy. Add a dedicated structural event/zone ledger where the source calls for it.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Require the complete frozen profile interval before start_date, or maintain developing snapshots with individual timestamps. Missing granular volume/profile inputs block the profile branch; do not synthesize them from daily high/low.

Retain prior structural levels and enough bars for right-side pivot confirmation. A level’s origin date and first-known date differ. Missing prior swings make the setup ineligible; do not pick future extrema to complete a pattern.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

**Volume-by-price evidence:** Show profile range/bins, POC/VAH/VAL as known, touch/reclaim/acceptance events and failures. Test a profile that changes late: earlier decisions must retain the old levels.

**Swings evidence:** Log pivot origin and confirmation, protected-level updates and every failed or stale candidate. Change bars after a decision and assert identical prior levels/signals. Backdated chart labels must never become backdated fills.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and limitations

Value-area percentage, profile rows/feed, session timezone, initial setup, significance/depth thresholds, swing algorithm, exact stop boundary, size and trade cap remain open. The narration’s generic BOS definition is imprecise, so use its actual higher-high/lower-low examples. A retrospective recovery sequence does not mean every losing reversal has a winning opposite trade.

### Writeup: Keep the available lesson complete without inventing the missing part

The later claim of three combined strategies is not evidence that this file teaches all three. The POC-bounce algorithm and original configuration are explicitly unavailable here. The two available branches still need a precedence/re-entry policy to avoid hindsight: record when a reversal became eligible, when it failed, and only then when a fresh breakout state satisfied its own conditions.

**Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

# Wyckoff-style spring and upthrust, with later breakout-pullback alternatives

Source: [FiboGhost X RNS](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1KRaUyCnFG/). Downloaded duration: 477.03 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

FiboGhost X RNS describes accumulation, advancing, distribution and declining phases, then trades false range breaks: a spring below support for longs and an upthrust above resistance for shorts. It is a simplified Wyckoff-style presentation rather than the full historical methodology.

## How to use or reproduce the source

1. Identify a range after the relevant prior directional move; the source associates accumulation with a prior decline and distribution with a prior rise.
2. Spring: price breaks below support and a candle closes back inside. Enter on the confirming close, stop below that candle/sweep, target the next level.
3. If the spring entry is missed, wait for a later break above range resistance and a pullback; stop below the pullback candle and require at least 2R. If no pullback, stay out under this variant.
4. Upthrust: price breaks above range resistance and closes back inside. The illustrated short enters on that confirming close, stops above the candle and targets the next level.
5. If missed, wait for the later support breakdown and pullback for the bearish continuation alternative.

## Missing rules and limitations

The phrase breakout candle must mean the false-break/reclaim candle in the immediate-entry branch, not an earlier unconfirmed candle outside the range. Range boundaries, close timing, stop buffer, minimum reward in the immediate branch, size and expiry remain open. A small risk relative to reward does not alone prove profitability. Neither a spring nor a range proves intentional manipulation or actual institutional accumulation.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

36–145s phases; 153–250s spring; 258–311s bullish breakout/retest alternative; 321–390s upthrust; 394–466s bearish alternative and no-pullback rule.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of complete machine transcript, caption and original chart evidence.

Machine transcripts may misrecognize names, numbers, and music. Settings and claims that could not be established are identified above. Any implementation examples added in this writeup are research choices, not extra rules attributed to the video.

sources.overview: Jaime Avalos gives three steps for a buy: sweep a previous low, break upward to a higher high, then retrace to retest the broken level. The caption emphasizes setting risk and objective before entry.
sources.gaps: The narration places the stop below the manipulation/sweep low, but the illustrated risk rectangle sits much nearer the retest/broken-high region and does not extend to that earlier sweep low. Resolve this stop-location mismatch before calculating 3R. Timeframe, instrument, close-versus-wick BOS, retest tolerance, buffer, order type and expiry are not fixed. The sweep is an observed price pattern; the claim that it supplies mandatory institutional fuel is an interpretation. A retest may fail or never occur.

# Sweep a prior low, break upward structure, and buy the retest at 3R

Source: [Jaime Avalos](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/14wbGHLSzTB/). Downloaded duration: 62.233 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Jaime Avalos gives three steps for a buy: sweep a previous low, break upward to a higher high, then retrace to retest the broken level. The caption emphasizes setting risk and objective before entry.

## How to use or reproduce the source

1. Mark the prior low and upper structural reference before the setup.
2. Wait for the low-side sweep.
3. Require the later upward break that exceeds the prior high.
4. Do not chase the initial break; wait for price to return to the broken level.
5. The candidate long enters on that retest, stop beneath the manipulation/sweep low, target three times the entry-to-stop distance.
6. Set size from that risk distance before submitting any order.

## Missing rules and limitations

The narration places the stop below the manipulation/sweep low, but the illustrated risk rectangle sits much nearer the retest/broken-high region and does not extend to that earlier sweep low. Resolve this stop-location mismatch before calculating 3R. Timeframe, instrument, close-versus-wick BOS, retest tolerance, buffer, order type and expiry are not fixed. The sweep is an observed price pattern; the claim that it supplies mandatory institutional fuel is an interpretation. A retest may fail or never occur.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

0–17s low sweep; 19–35s upward break; 35–52s retest, sweep-low stop and 3R; the caption restates the steps.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of complete machine transcript, caption and original chart evidence.

# External swing trend versus a small internal lower low

Source: [Lewis Kelly Trades](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1CHxCqeqKC/). Downloaded duration: 23.722 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Lewis Kelly Trades warns that a small bearish move inside a broader bullish swing can be internal structure. It advises marking external swings before shorting an apparent local lower low.

## How to use or reproduce the source

1. Choose the structural scale and mark its confirmed major highs/lows.
2. Identify the bullish protected low at that scale.
3. Compare a smaller lower low with that major reference rather than automatically relabeling the whole trend bearish.
4. Keep internal and external structures as separate labels.
5. Add a separate entry/risk model; the clip only teaches hierarchy.

## Missing rules and limitations

External is not numerically defined, and no pivot delay, timeframe, trade trigger, stop, target or size is supplied. The advice to ignore all small moves is an opinion; some strategies deliberately trade them. A broader uptrend can eventually fail, so protected levels need a clear invalidation rule.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

The complete twenty-four-second narration contrasts a small lower low with an intact larger bullish swing.

# An eight-pattern glossary for visual recognition

Source: [Tradex](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1cVx23Sym7/). Downloaded duration: 5.038 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The static chart-pattern glossary names ascending triangle, descending triangle, bull flag, bear flag, cup and handle, head and shoulders, double top and rounding bottom. Small schematic arrows indicate the conventional illustrated direction, not guaranteed outcomes.

## How to use or reproduce the source

1. Ascending triangle: flat resistance with rising lows; descending triangle: flat support with falling highs.
2. Bull/bear flags: a directional impulse followed by a smaller corrective channel.
3. Cup and handle: rounded recovery and smaller pullback near the rim.
4. Head and shoulders: three peaks with a higher middle peak and neckline.
5. Double top: two upper tests and intervening support.
6. Rounding bottom: a broad curved base.
7. Identify a completed break/confirmation separately from a developing resemblance, then define entry, invalidation, objective and size.

## Missing rules and limitations

The five-second reference gives no numerical shape tolerances, timeframe, volume rules, stop or test sample. It is useful for vocabulary and replay annotation, but recognition alone is not a validated strategy. Bearish and bullish failures must remain in any study.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

All original samples show the same eight labeled schematic patterns.

# RSI cheat sheet: extreme levels, regular divergence, and trendline breaks

Source: [Ashish Kumar](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1HCKCQssap/). Downloaded duration: 6.477 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The infographic has three paired ideas: RSI below30/above70, bullish/bearish regular divergence, and aligned breaks of price/RSI trendlines. These are different observations, not one automatically validated system.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Extreme-level panels call RSI<30 oversold and RSI>70 overbought. Treat them as conditions rather than immediate orders.
2. Bullish divergence: price makes a lower low while RSI makes a higher low. Bearish: price makes a higher high while RSI makes a lower high. Match the same swing times.
3. The bottom examples draw trendlines on price and RSI and illustrate a break in the intended direction.
4. Choose one explicit trigger and define pivot confirmation, stop and exit before testing.
5. Do not combine all panels after seeing which predicted the selected outcome.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

RSI length/source, timeframe, pivot lag, trendline anchors, buffer, target and size are absent. RSI can stay extreme during a trend. The slogan about spotting reversals before they happen is not demonstrated by static schematics. A divergence requires later pivot confirmation under many implementations.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

The original full-size cheat sheet was inspected for 30/70, the two divergence definitions and the lower price/RSI trendline panels.

Reviewed using: manual inspection of original sampled frames, recognized chart text and saved caption; music is not treated as instruction.

# Breakout entry versus waiting for a pullback

Source: [FinShala with Priya](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1JvhZLRQcS/). Downloaded duration: 5.04 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

FinShala with Priya’s static image compares an immediate resistance breakout with a later return to the broken level. It calls the first more aggressive and the second more conservative, while acknowledging that a pullback may never occur.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Mark the prior resistance before the break.
2. Breakout branch: define a close/penetration trigger above it and act only after that event.
3. Pullback branch: let the break occur, wait for a return toward old resistance/new support, then require a declared confirmation.
4. Keep each branch’s missed opportunities and failures separate.
5. Add invalidation, target, size and expiry; the source does not supply them.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

## Local evidence and reproducibility

# Three breakout contexts: downtrend reversal, double top, and distribution break

Source: [FX PULSE](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1CRtxWWsUM/). Downloaded duration: 5.04 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

FX PULSE’s static worksheet combines an upward downtrend-line break/higher low, a later double-top neckline reversal, and a subsequent distribution-range breakdown. Smaller diagrams explicitly separate the three contexts.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. For the initial bullish reversal, identify the declining structure and the break that later holds a higher low.
2. For the double top, mark both peaks and the intervening neckline; the bearish break is a different setup.
3. For distribution continuation, mark the sideways lower range and its eventual downside break.
4. Preserve each reference before the respective event.
5. Define separate triggers, stops, targets and sizes instead of treating the whole idealized path as one prediction.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

No instrument, timeframe, close/retest rule, zone tolerance, buffer or tested sample is supplied. The worksheet compresses selected successful transitions into one story; actual ranges can break either way and a double top can fail.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

All original samples show Mastering Breakout Trading and the three labeled lower panels.

# Integration plan: Pro Scalper tool selection and selected signal/target regions

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `8dbe9ea48fdd661108c02239e23b56aa28e65cd3806553b6e1e3e71be84b4822`.

## Experiment overview

Profit Pro searches Pro Scalper, then shows red/green signals, trend bands and boxed risk/reward-style areas on selected charts. The reel invites trying the tool without disclosing its mechanics.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Start with a specification/prospective-signal capture study. The shown tool, selected recap or undisclosed model does not yet define a reproducible trading engine. Obtain its exact revision, inputs and as-issued signals before enabling a faithful performance run; a public-formula proxy must have a separate experiment identity.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to use or reproduce it

1. Select the exact Pro Scalper version and record inputs.
2. Establish first signal availability and whether labels revise.
3. Capture entry, stop and target values prospectively rather than inferring them from completed rectangles.
4. Define position size, exit priority, repeat-signal handling and expiry.
5. Evaluate all signals and costs across later data.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Create a source-specific adapter for the sequence in the Rules and inputs section, preserving the order in which each illustrated reference and confirmation becomes known. Store candidate, armed, confirmed, expired and invalidated events separately. [patterns/base_pattern.py](../../patterns/base_pattern.py) supplies signal/annotation structures, while [indicators/_signal.py](../../indicators/_signal.py) demonstrates latest-bar output; neither supplies the missing source rules. A recap or undisclosed indicator stays blocked until its actual generator and execution specification are available.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

For the initial incomplete-specification state, report the missing dependencies and any captured configuration/signal evidence; trading metrics remain unavailable. Product slogans, floating P&L, dashboards and selected chart rectangles are not validated performance.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and evidence limits

No formula, full setting set, timeframe policy, executed ledger or audited expectancy is supplied. A historical buy/sell marker and target box are chart objects, not proof of a real filled order. The music token is not instruction.

**Practical next step:** Obtain the exact script/model revision, complete inputs/formulas or lawful timestamped as-issued signals, and its entry/exit/size contract. Capture changing-bar and repaint behavior prospectively. Until then, keep the faithful performance run disabled; use an explicitly named proxy only after specifying its differences.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

# A buy-or-sell quiz resolved with a rising-channel continuation example

Source: [Trade_the_forex](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1MEcVeAk1m/). Downloaded duration: 9.7 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

1. Identify the upward swing and its current pullback.
2. Preserve any rising-channel anchors before future bars.
3. The final example favors continuation from the lower/support area, with risk below and reward higher.
4. Supply an actual rejection/close trigger rather than treating the countdown as a decision rule.

# Volatility Gated Supertrend with ATR 17 and multiplier 4

Source: [TRADING CHART](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1E4eUkaZ7D/). Downloaded duration: 29.977 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The reel selects Volatility Gated Supertrend [BackQuant], claims it filters chop, and demonstrates buy signals and partial-profit lines. The search screen clarifies the author/name misrecognized in speech.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Select the exact BackQuant script/version.
2. Set ATR multiplier 4 and ATR length 17 as narrated.
3. The stated action is long on a buy signal.
4. Take partial profits when price reaches the displayed target lines, but define quantity allocation and what happens to the remaining stop separately.
5. Supply initial invalidation, exit priority, size and signal timing before testing.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The 17.04s panel shows Volatility Gate checked, Fast ATR 7, Slow ATR 50 and Gate Threshold 0.75, with Show Signals, Trend Fill and Show Gate Status checked. The gate formula, target calculations, full inputs, timeframe and complete short mirror are not disclosed. A partial-profit instruction without quantities does not define realized results. The chop-filter and best-indicator claims are not independently validated.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

4–19s script/input setup; 23–30s long and partial target lines; original search screen confirms BackQuant.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of full short transcript, caption and original chart evidence.

[Downloaded video](video.mp4) · [Page description](video.description) · [Timestamped machine transcript](transcript.txt) · [Sampled frames](frames/contact-sheet.jpg) · [Metadata](video.info.json) · [Integrity record](source.json)

Machine transcripts may misrecognize names, numbers, and music. Settings and claims that could not be established are identified above. Any implementation examples added in this writeup are research choices, not extra rules attributed to the video.

# Integration plan: Volatility Gated Supertrend with ATR 17 and multiplier 4

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `1aea86e98f6a326f6dc29ddc9aec73ac512cc560196a725e8a3446f25547a558`.

## Experiment overview

The reel selects Volatility Gated Supertrend [BackQuant], claims it filters chop, and demonstrates buy signals and partial-profit lines. The search screen clarifies the author/name misrecognized in speech.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Evaluate the particular setup or indicator sequence described here on a frozen historical universe. First produce causal features and candidate events; promote it to a trade simulation only after the unresolved entry, invalidation, exit and sizing decisions below have an explicit versioned specification. A daily-equity adaptation must be labeled when the source uses another interval or product.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to use or reproduce it

1. Select the exact BackQuant script/version.
2. Set ATR multiplier 4 and ATR length 17 as narrated.
3. The stated action is long on a buy signal.
4. Take partial profits when price reaches the displayed target lines, but define quantity allocation and what happens to the remaining stop separately.
5. Supply initial invalidation, exit priority, size and signal timing before testing.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

[indicators/vol_gated_supertrend.py](../../indicators/vol_gated_supertrend.py) matches ATR17×4 and gate fast7/slow50/.75, but assumes fast/slow ATR ratio and a trailing-line exit. The writeup does not disclose the gate or target formula; verify parity and define partial quantities instead of presenting the repository translation as exact source code.

**Supertrend:** [indicators/_math.py](../../indicators/_math.py) supplies Wilder ATR and Supertrend bands, while [indicators/supertrend.py](../../indicators/supertrend.py) is one concrete preset. Match ATR seeding, price source, band ratchets and flip versus persistent state. An oscillator, confluence dashboard or proprietary gate needs its own verified formula.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Warm ATR17 and gate fastATR7/slowATR50, including previous-state comparisons. The existing60-bar minimum is a comparison baseline to verify, not a source guarantee.

Warm ATR, recursive bands and prior-state comparisons. Keep startup and maximum history cap explicit; a source’s unspecified defaults cannot be filled from another writeup without an assumption.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

**Supertrend evidence:** Compare band values and first signal availability on deterministic prefixes, including whipsaws and gate rejection. Test source-specific settings independently from existing module defaults.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and evidence limits

The 17.04s panel shows Volatility Gate checked, Fast ATR 7, Slow ATR 50 and Gate Threshold 0.75, with Show Signals, Trend Fill and Show Gate Status checked. The gate formula, target calculations, full inputs, timeframe and complete short mirror are not disclosed. A partial-profit instruction without quantities does not define realized results. The chop-filter and best-indicator claims are not independently validated.

**Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

# A bearish structure shift and return to an upper POI: a paired schematic/chart

Source: [Zahid FX](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1FRcxak88M/). Downloaded duration: 15.0 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Zahid FX’s static SMC Gold Expert image pairs a bearish schematic with a selected chart. It shows initial bullish breaks, a later bearish MSS/BOS, a return toward a high-side POI and a short rectangle aimed lower.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Separate the early bullish expansion from the later bearish structure change.
2. Mark the overhead POI associated with the earlier upper region/departure.
3. Wait for the illustrated return into that POI after the bearish shift.
4. The drawing places risk above the POI and reward toward the lower prior extreme.
5. Define an actual confirmation, stop buffer, size and expiry independently.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The silent image does not reliably establish instrument/feed, numeric timeframe, exact prices, pivot algorithm or order timing. VIP emojis and a schematic matching a selected chart do not validate high probability or realized performance.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

All original samples show the same paired bearish schematic/chart and upper POI short rectangle.

Reviewed using: manual inspection of original sampled frames, recognized chart text and saved caption; music is not treated as instruction.

# A holy-grail claim over selected indicator risk/reward boxes

Source: [ZynAlgo](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/16YeAJutvY7/). Downloaded duration: 15.466 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

ZynAlgo displays alternating buy/sell markers and colored entry/stop/target-style boxes while calling the tool a holy grail. It does not provide a mathematical or operational definition of the signals.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Identify the exact product/version and inputs.
2. Record a new signal and all levels before revealing later prices.
3. Distinguish chart drawings from actual broker orders.
4. Define size, exit priority, repeat signals and expiry.
5. Evaluate every eligible signal, with costs and drawdown, rather than only the montage.

# Bull flag: aggressive lower-channel entry versus confirmed upper break

Source: [Forex School](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/19j1D4Trxr/). Downloaded duration: 15.0 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Forex School’s silent graphic and detailed caption define an upward flagpole, a smaller descending corrective channel, and an upward breakout. Two entries are explicitly offered, with a flagpole-height objective.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Identify the prior impulsive upward leg.
2. Draw the downward flag channel during the correction.
3. Aggressive branch: enter near the flag’s lower boundary/retracement. This anticipates the break and needs its own invalidation.
4. Confirmed branch: wait for price to break the upper trendline, then apply a declared close/retest order rule.
5. Project the flagpole height upward from the chosen breakout reference for the displayed objective.
6. Evaluate the two entries separately, retaining different fills, stops and missed opportunities.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The caption calls the second safer, but it can still fail and usually has a different price/risk. Instrument, timeframe, flag slope/duration, confirmation, stop, buffer, size and expiry are not specified. The reliability claim is not supported by a full sample.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

All original samples show the same Bull Flag diagram with Entry1/Entry2 and pole-based target; the full caption explains both branches.

Reviewed using: manual inspection of original sampled frames, recognized chart text and saved caption; music is not treated as instruction.

Source: [Mananjay Capital](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1bTkwNxMzx/). Downloaded duration: 5.04 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Use the paired reversals to compare peak/trough structure and neckline direction.
2. Use flags to separate an impulse from its smaller correction.
3. Use triangles/wedges to identify flat versus converging boundaries and their slopes.
4. Treat each displayed breakout arrow as a condition that must occur, not a prediction from an incomplete silhouette.
5. Select one family, define quantitative geometry/confirmation, then add risk and exits before testing.

All original samples show the same twelve-panel pattern sheet.

# BOS, range liquidity, a rising liquidity line, and Fibonacci entry refinement

Source: [Xauusd.zz](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1HTRfxijQi/). Downloaded duration: 19.087 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Xauusd.zz illustrates an upward BOS, a sideways range whose highs are marked as liquidity, rising local support/liquidity, and a lower Fibonacci-refined long region. The final position drawing targets above the range and reveals a rally.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Mark the bullish BOS and range boundaries before the retracement.
2. Identify the upper range-liquidity objective and lower rising line separately.
3. Preserve the impulse anchors used by the Fibonacci drawing.
4. The candidate long is in the lower Entry Long band, stop beneath it and upper target beyond range liquidity.
5. The original 5.40s frame highlights the lower band between 0.618 and 0.786 on a Fibonacci scale with 0 at the impulse high and 1 at the low. The later Entry Long box occupies that band. The 0.382 line is an intermediate reference, not the entry shown. Choose an exact price within the band and a confirmation policy before implementing.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

No timeframe, instrument, precise within-band entry, pivot rule, stop buffer, size or expiry is supplied. A line called liquidity does not show actual stop inventory. The final favorable chart does not prove the earlier range would break upward.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Original samples show BOS+Liquidity+Fib, Range Liquidity, rising line, Entry Long/Stop-loss and upper Target.

Reviewed using: manual inspection of original sampled frames, recognized chart text and saved caption; music is not treated as instruction.

Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

1. Mark the declining structure and its descending line before the break.
2. Observe the local bullish break and later higher-low formation.
3. Mark the rising support/retest confluence.
4. Check the pictured Stochastic RSI oversold condition.

# Support/resistance with candle rejection, repeated touches, and role reversal

Source: [MrTrader NK](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/19aFhbgdG8/). Downloaded duration: 8.01 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

MrTrader NK’s notebook sheet defines support/resistance, shows long lower/upper rejection wicks, repeated level tests, breakout/retest behavior and an hourly XAUUSD example. It is a foundational chart-reading reference.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Mark prior reaction zones before a new approach.
2. At support, observe rejection of lower prices; at resistance, rejection of higher prices.
3. Keep a wick rejection distinct from a completed breakout.
4. After a break, watch whether former support acts as resistance or former resistance as support.
5. Use candle confirmation and trend context, then define the actual entry, invalidation, objective and size separately.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The sheet asserts more touches make a level stronger, but repeated tests can also precede failure; touch count is a hypothesis to test, not a law. No zone-width rule, minimum separation, candle ratio, order timing, buffer or risk fraction is provided. The XAUUSD1h chart is an example, not current gold guidance.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

The full original sheet and OCR show definitions, wick examples, repeated touches, retest/flip and the hourly gold chart.

Reviewed using: manual inspection of original sampled frames, recognized chart text and saved caption; music is not treated as instruction.

# Bullish butterfly-style XABCD drawing and a lower-point long

Source: [Trader Dhana](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/19okVqsMej/). Downloaded duration: 12.499 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Trader Dhana overlays a five-point harmonic butterfly shape on a selected chart, with the final D point below the earlier X and a later rally. The small reference diagram contains Fibonacci ratios, including a visible.786 reference, but the full leg mapping/tolerances are not explained.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Mark the alternating X,A,B,C,D pivots only when confirmed.
2. Measure each leg with consistent anchors before accepting the named harmonic pattern.
3. Do not infer exact ratio ranges from a similar textbook butterfly; verify the source diagram/code if implementing this version.
4. The illustrated long is at the lower D region, risk beneath it and reward toward an upper swing.
5. Define a reversal trigger, target, buffer and size independently.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The 3.53s original frame makes the ratios legible. The reference shows AB/XA 0.786, BC/AB 0.382–0.886, CD/BC 1.618–2.24 and AD/XA 1.27. The worked drawing instead displays 0.848, 0.69, 1.849 and 1.345 respectively, so it is not an exact match to the fixed 0.786/1.27 reference values. No allowed tolerance is stated. Its target is near A, but the clip does not establish a general exit, timeframe, instrument or pivot delay. A five-point drawing can be fitted retrospectively. The selected rally does not prove harmonic completion guarantees reversal.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Original samples show the Bullish Butterfly reference, XABCD overlay, lower Entry Long region and later selected rally.
