Source: [Wealth Max Capital](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1FbVrEJJ38/). Downloaded duration: 19.851 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

WealthMax’s silent clip credits LuxAlgo and displays Signals and Overlays 6.0.2 on a five-minute June 2023 S&P 500 futures chart (the opening header shows 500 FUTURES and prices near 4137; the cropped later header does not establish Nasdaq 100). The visible menu includes Swing Trader and Contrarian Trader presets and filter names such as Smart Trail, Neo Cloud, Trend Tracer and Trend Strength. The chart then shows colored trail/cloud regions and buy/sell-style markers around selected moves. The subject is configuring a commercial chart overlay, not a disclosed standalone mathematical strategy.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Identify Signals and Overlays 6.0.2 and the historical instrument/contract shown before attempting comparison with another revision.
2. Save the full actual preset and input values; the presence of a filter name in a menu does not prove that every listed filter is enabled.
3. Note whether a marker occurs on an unfinished bar, at close or only after later confirmation.
4. Define how markers and any trail interact with a protective stop and final exit.
5. Replay an uninterrupted sample and retain changed, losing and missing signals alongside the selected examples.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The clip does not establish every enabled filter or parameter, the precise entry algorithm, initial risk, position size or target rules. Historical signals and a favorable cloud/trail relationship do not verify real-time behavior or net returns. The chart’s June 2023 futures context is historical; contract rollover and feed differences matter when reproducing it. No current subscription terms or performance promise is verified. A reproduction should be explicit about version differences rather than assuming a newer preset is identical.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

The opening frame shows 500 FUTURES (JUN 2023), 5 m, CME_MINI and prices near 4137, supporting the S&P 500 identification rather than Nasdaq 100. Later frames show Signals&Overlays 6.0.2, with preset/filter names and selected chart signals.

Reviewed using: manual inspection of original chart/settings frames and the complete saved caption; music is not treated as instruction.

sources.title: Ultimate Bias PRO alignment of swing and internal structure
sources.overview: Algoryze’s Spanish demonstration uses Ultimate Bias PRO to compare swing structure with internal structure. Its central rule is alignment: wait while the two directions disagree, and look for the directional opportunity once they match. The pictured conflict has bullish swing structure but bearish internal structure; a later bullish alignment leads to a drawn long with the swing high as the objective. The dashboard is intended to make different structural scales easier to compare.
sources.gaps: The source does not disclose the underlying pivot formulas, confirmation delays, full inputs or exact entry/stop criteria. A swing-high destination is not a guaranteed target fill, particularly if that high has already changed by the decision time. Assertions about knowing the next move exactly are promotional, not measured predictive certainty. The selected bullish example does not validate a mirrored short rule or establish how often the two scales disagree, align too late or whipsaw. Causal replay is necessary to distinguish live dashboard states from final historical labels.

# Ultimate Bias PRO alignment of swing and internal structure

Source: [Algoryze Connected Page](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1ZK26MGdGq/). Downloaded duration: 28.721 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Algoryze’s Spanish demonstration uses Ultimate Bias PRO to compare swing structure with internal structure. Its central rule is alignment: wait while the two directions disagree, and look for the directional opportunity once they match. The pictured conflict has bullish swing structure but bearish internal structure; a later bullish alignment leads to a drawn long with the swing high as the objective. The dashboard is intended to make different structural scales easier to compare.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Identify the exact Ultimate Bias PRO version and its swing/internal sensitivity settings.
2. Observe the two dashboard states at the same decision time.
3. Under the pictured bullish branch, stand aside while swing is up and internal is down.
4. When both become bullish, evaluate the source’s long scenario toward the relevant swing high.
5. Define whether alignment itself triggers an order or whether a break/retest is required, then add stop, size, expiry and cost assumptions.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The source does not disclose the underlying pivot formulas, confirmation delays, full inputs or exact entry/stop criteria. A swing-high destination is not a guaranteed target fill, particularly if that high has already changed by the decision time. Assertions about knowing the next move exactly are promotional, not measured predictive certainty. The selected bullish example does not validate a mirrored short rule or establish how often the two scales disagree, align too late or whipsaw. Causal replay is necessary to distinguish live dashboard states from final historical labels.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Complete 28.7 s Spanish narration discusses swing/internal alignment and the swing-high target; original frames show mismatched then aligned dashboard states and the selected long.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of the complete saved transcript and caption with inspection of original chart frames; OCR checked against the images where material.

# Low-volume pullback into EMA or VWAP, with a close-below exit

Source: [Anand I SEBI Reg RA](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1NBymTwq2x/). Downloaded duration: 5.04 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Anand’s poster describes a long continuation setup rather than buying every downward candle. Price is already rising, pulls back toward an EMA or VWAP on lower volume, then resumes upward. The volume diagram circles the quiet pullback and shows volume increasing on the subsequent breakout. The printed exit is price closing below VWAP and EMA. That exit instruction is a substantive part of this particular poster and should be retained separately from its entry location.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Establish an upward trend before classifying the retracement.
2. Mark the EMA and VWAP used on the chart and observe a return toward either reference.
3. Compare the pullback volume with a reference defined in advance; the image does not quantify low volume.
4. Wait for the stated resumption of the uptrend, with the illustrated increase in breakout volume. Define the actual trigger rather than assuming the first touch is sufficient.
5. Track the printed close-below-VWAP-and-EMA exit; decide how both-reference wording is evaluated on completed bars.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The poster omits EMA length/source, VWAP anchoring, timeframe, session, volume threshold and resumption formula. There is no initial protective stop, target or risk fraction. A close-based exit does not cap losses during gaps or before a bar completes. The EMA-or-VWAP entry and VWAP-and-EMA exit are different logical conditions; they should not be collapsed into one generic moving-average touch rule. Low-volume pullbacks can fail, and the single favorable drawing provides no measured edge.

All original static frames show Pull Back on Low Volume, entry at EMA/VWAP, increased breakout volume and an exit on a close below VWAP&EMA.

# Five kettlebell exercises advertised as fifty repetitions each day

Source: [Antwan Rarcus](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1Fh1HK34AH/). Downloaded duration: 28.373 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

AntwanRarcus demonstrates five movements with one kettlebell: rotational swings, halos, around-the-world passes, standard swings and standing horizontal presses. The narration proposes fifty repetitions of each daily, totaling 250 repetitions, and associates the moves with a tighter waist, defined core, rounder shoulders and fuller chest. The original frames show the standing press pushing the bell away from the chest; it is not a bench press. This is fitness content included in the URL list.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Identify the five distinct patterns before attempting the advertised circuit.
2. Rotational swing: the demonstration moves the bell across the front of the body with coordinated trunk/hip movement. Halos pass it around the head using both hands.
3. Around-the-world passes move the bell around the waist with controlled hand changes. Standard swings use a hip hinge to send the bell forward.
4. The standing horizontal press starts near the chest, moves the bell outward and returns it under control.
5. Treat the fifty-per-movement daily prescription as the creator’s proposal, not an individualized starting dose. Learn unloaded/light patterns, establish a secure grip and stop a set when control deteriorates. The source does not specify load, rest or a progression.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The clip does not define whether fifty is total or per direction for asymmetric movements, and it supplies no sets, tempo, recovery plan or suitability assessment. Appearance changes are not established by the demonstration. Training a body region does not selectively remove its fat; [ACE’s fitness-myth guidance](https://www.acefitness.org/about-ace/press-room/press-releases/319/ace-lists-most-common-fitness-myths/) rejects spot reduction. For the ordinary swing, [ACE’s technique lesson](https://www.acefitness.org/continuing-education/certified/january-2025/8788/the-ace-do-it-better-series-the-two-handed-kettlebell-swing/) starts with a proper hip hinge. That reference does not validate every rotational variation or the daily 250-repetition dose. No trading method appears.

## Local evidence and reproducibility

0–6 s rotational swings; approximately 6–12 s halos;12–18 s around-the-world;18–23 s swings;23–28 s standing horizontal presses. Full narration repeatedly says 50 daily; caption gives 250 reps/five exercises.

sources.title: Exhaustion Mean Theory as a five-condition mean-reversion checklist

# Exhaustion Mean Theory as a five-condition mean-reversion checklist

Source: [G Street Trades](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1FEf1URMPy/). Downloaded duration: 60.627 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

GStreetTrades calls the framework EMT, Exhaustion Mean Theory, and lists five pillars for fading an extended move. Price first accelerates away from a mean, then stalls or rejects. A footprint is used to look for buyer effort without further upward result. The distance back to the mean should offer worthwhile reward relative to the proposed risk. Finally, a liquidity sweep is used as context for a failed breakout/trapped-trader interpretation. The pictured trade is a short fade after an upward extension.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Define the mean and measure the extension from it; this reel does not name a specific EMA or VWAP setting.
2. Observe the described exhaustion rather than shorting merely because price has risen.
3. Inspect the footprint for the stated effort-versus-result mismatch, using an explicit measure chosen before the outcome.
4. Compare the return-to-mean objective with the actual invalidation distance and costs. The narration proposes roughly 0.5–1 R risk for 3+ R reward, but does not define the common risk unit or exact price levels; do not convert this directly into an account-risk percentage.
5. Check for the illustrated sweep and then specify the actionable trigger, protective order and size separately.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The clip does not quantify acceleration, exhaustion, footprint imbalance or sweep, and it does not disclose a complete entry/stop algorithm. Its reward/risk wording should not be mistaken for a specified entry-to-stop distance in price units. A footprint can support an interpretation but does not identify particular trapped institutions or guarantee reversal; an extended trend may continue. Claims about prop firms wanting a ban, funding totals and most traders losing are promotional assertions without supporting records here. No prohibition or proven success rate is established by the video.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Complete 60.6 s narration lists acceleration, exhaustion, footprint confirmation, distance from mean and liquidity sweep; original frames show the five-pillar title and selected short/mean-return diagram.

Reviewed using: manual synthesis of the complete saved transcript and caption with inspection of original chart frames; OCR checked against the images where material.

Machine transcripts may misrecognize names, numbers, and music. Settings and claims that could not be established are identified above. Any implementation examples added in this writeup are research choices, not extra rules attributed to the video.

# Integration plan: Exhaustion Mean Theory as a five-condition mean-reversion checklist

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `4a402d97e9f228408b5418911a74a0ae17adb1f9be320ef3a3f8bb1a1ca65e0c`.

Finally, a liquidity sweep is used as context for a failed breakout/trapped-trader interpretation. The pictured trade is a short fade after an upward extension.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Evaluate the particular setup or indicator sequence described here on a frozen historical universe. First produce causal features and candidate events; promote it to a trade simulation only after the unresolved entry, invalidation, exit and sizing decisions below have an explicit versioned specification. A daily-equity adaptation must be labeled when the source uses another interval or product.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Keep the five-condition Exhaustion Mean Theory checklist separate from item169’s EMA9/VWAP recipe. This writeup does not define the mean and includes footprint information, so obtain its own feature/data specification.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and evidence limits

The clip does not quantify acceleration, exhaustion, footprint imbalance or sweep, and it does not disclose a complete entry/stop algorithm. Its reward/risk wording should not be mistaken for a specified entry-to-stop distance in price units. A footprint can support an interpretation but does not identify particular trapped institutions or guarantee reversal; an extended trend may continue. Claims about prop firms wanting a ban, funding totals and most traders losing are promotional assertions without supporting records here. No prohibition or proven success rate is established by the video.

**Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

Source: [Harlan Trades](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1DUpQ8AnKt/). Downloaded duration: 29.866 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

HarlanTrades profiles an upward swing rather than only a sideways consolidation. 1. Identify the completed higher-low/higher-high leg without using a future turning point.

3. Mark its POC and preserve it as price retraces.
4. Observe the narrated reaction at the level in the direction of the pre-existing higher-timeframe bias.
5. Define the exact entry trigger, invalidation, target and risk before replaying the continuation.

There is no need to join a group to study the chart concept, and historical volume concentration does not prove remaining buy orders.

sources.overview: MarkCogar’s silent montage advertises a 15-minute kettlebell workout and shows three exercise segments. The first is labeled KB Swing Squat; the next combines a clean/halo-style movement, although its edited label is misspelled/unclear; the last is KB Pop Squat. The visible prescriptions repeatedly read 3 rounds|30 sec. The opening half-kneeling image is promotional imagery, while the main demonstration is a standing circuit. This URL contains fitness content, not chart analysis.
sources.gaps: Three exercises for 30 seconds across three rounds account for 4.5 minutes of work, so the title’s 15 minutes cannot be reconstructed from the shown timing alone. No bell weight, side changes, rest, warmup, progression or landing instruction is given. The fast-fat-burning claim is not measured by this montage. [ACE’s swing lesson](https://www.acefitness.org/continuing-education/certified/january-2025/8788/the-ace-do-it-better-series-the-two-handed-kettlebell-swing/) emphasizes learning a hip hinge; it does not establish that the pictured squat/swing combination or fast loaded pop squat is appropriate for every viewer. Treat the montage as movement identification, not a complete beginner coaching program.

# Short kettlebell circuit montage labeled as a fifteen-minute workout

Source: [Mark Cogar](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1DgQSNtvkm/). Downloaded duration: 15.041 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

MarkCogar’s silent montage advertises a 15-minute kettlebell workout and shows three exercise segments. The first is labeled KB Swing Squat; the next combines a clean/halo-style movement, although its edited label is misspelled/unclear; the last is KB Pop Squat. The visible prescriptions repeatedly read 3 rounds|30 sec. The opening half-kneeling image is promotional imagery, while the main demonstration is a standing circuit. This URL contains fitness content, not chart analysis.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. First separate the segments: the swing-squat moves between a squat and a forward-held/swinging bell; the middle segment lifts a low bell toward the upper body and includes a pass near the head; the pop squat holds the bell near the chest while rising briskly from a squat.

# Three illustrated contexts for a bullish order-block retest

Source: [MrTrader NK](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1KT9qBwu2Q/). Downloaded duration: 8.0 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

MrTraderNK’s static reference is titled Types of Bullish Order Block Retest. It presents three rows: continuation pattern, consolidation and buy-side liquidity. The labels describe contexts around a bullish demand-area return; this is not a breaker-block lesson despite tags that might suggest broader smart-money topics.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. In the continuation row, identify the prior upward structure and the pullback toward the marked demand zone.
2. In the consolidation row, identify the sideways pause above the zone and the illustrated return before an upward departure.
3. In the buy-side-liquidity row, distinguish the marked prior highs from the demand area below; the return and later upward path are separate events.

5. Specify what candle defines the block, when BOS is confirmed and what reaction permits entry, then add invalidation and objectives.

Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. Retain the zone-formation/impulse history before the chosen date range. A three-candle gap becomes known only after its third candle; a block validated by later displacement becomes available only after that validation. Missing formation history makes it unavailable.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

**Zones and gaps evidence:** Export original zone bounds, formation/availability, every return and invalidation. Test early touches before zone availability, overlapping zones, no-return moves and failed retests. Do not treat institutional-order narratives as OHLCV-observed facts.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and evidence limits

The poster gives no instrument, timeframe, block-boundary convention, pivot algorithm, entry price, stop, target or position size. Its circled reactions show selected outcomes and do not prove that the zone contains institutional orders. The buy-side-liquidity label is a reference to highs, not direct observation of everyone’s stops. A zone that fails or is revisited repeatedly needs an explicit lifecycle policy. Do not infer a guaranteed long, a mirrored short system or a numerical reward/risk from the illustration alone.

**Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. # Fixed-range volume profile, value-area rotation and weekly stock examples

Source: [Tarzan Trading TT](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1BwprXukSH/). Downloaded duration: 534.208 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

TarzanTradingTT gives a longer fixed-range volume-profile lesson. The tool is anchored from a recent low to a high, with POC, value-area high and value-area low enabled. POC is the highest-volume price bin; the value area represents approximately 70 percent of the selected volume, not 70 percent of the number of trades or a guarantee that price spends 70 percent of its future time there. The narration contrasts high-volume nodes, pictured around consolidation, with low-volume regions, pictured during faster movement.

The proposed rotation framework buys near/below VAL, takes a partial at POC and seeks VAH for the remainder. Its short branch starts above VAH, takes a partial at POC and seeks VAL. The weekly AMD example also combines a value-area-low region with drawn demand zones in a strong uptrend. Later it discusses a return from above VAH toward POC. A later example, narrated as Paramount, illustrates a short from above VAH, then a buy below VAL. However, the original frame at 524 seconds shows Advanced Micro Devices Inc · 1W · NASDAQ during that later sequence, so the montage does not consistently establish the security being described. These are historical applications of a volume-location hypothesis, not a documented sequence of live fills.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Select a completed low-to-high interval, record the timestamps and create a fixed-range profile. Enable POC, VAH and VAL and preserve its row/bin and volume-data settings.
2. Read the profile as a distribution of historical volume by price. Identify the actual 70 percent setting rather than assuming all platforms use the same value-area construction.
3. For the proposed long branch, locate price at or below VAL; the source’s targets are partial POC, remainder VAH. For the short branch, locate price above VAH; its targets are partial POC, remainder VAL.
4. Treat any AMD demand-zone overlap and prevailing trend as separate confluence requiring predeclared definitions.
5. Add an entry confirmation, protective invalidation, risk fraction, allocation between targets and maximum holding period. The lesson does not complete those rules.
6. Replay the weekly examples with only the profile information available at each historical decision. Test a frozen completed profile separately from one that keeps expanding.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The video uses cheap/expensive relative to the chosen historical distribution; these labels do not establish fundamental valuation, institutional ownership or an obligation to return to POC. # Inner trendline break, bearish CHoCH and return toward an upper POI

Source: [The Liquidity Mystery](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/19dx1q3NYW/). Downloaded duration: 19.86 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

The Liquidity Mystery’s silent animation builds a bearish example from an initially rising chart. It draws an Inner TL beneath the advance, marks a prior high that price exceeds, then shows a downward break of the diagonal and a horizontal CHoCH reference. A red POI is drawn around the upper reversal area. Price rebounds toward that region; a short risk/reward box has risk above and a blue objective below, near the marked SSL. The final sequence falls through that lower reference.

1. Draw the inner rising trendline from the demonstrated earlier lows before the break.
2. Mark the prior high and observe the later excursion above it.
3. Separate the diagonal-line break from the horizontal CHoCH event; they are different chart references.
4. Mark the upper POI and wait for the illustrated rebound toward it after the bearish shift.
5. Treat the later short toward sell-side liquidity as the source’s scenario, while specifying the actual entry test, stop buffer, target selection and size before replay.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

There is no spoken explanation or numerical price/time axis. The exact POI candle boundaries, CHoCH confirmation, trendline anchors and role of the small Imb-style annotation are not fully defined. The animation does not prove that a limit order at the red zone would fill or that a viewer could identify the reversal in advance. No timeframe, instrument, reward/risk ratio, risk fraction or expiry is supplied. The final selloff is selected evidence of one path, not validation that a trendline break plus POI return reliably predicts lower liquidity.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Original 0–6 s frames construct the inner trendline and prior-high reference;8–11 s labels CHoCH and POI;14–20 s adds the short drawing, lower SSL and final decline.

# Consolidation Range with Signals: breakout and range-fade branches

Source: [Trade Empire](https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1CHMQCdEiz/). Downloaded duration: 356.052 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

TradeEmpire demonstrates Consolidation Range with Signals by Zeiierman on an hourly GBPJPY example. The indicator is described as detecting weak-trend consolidation through ADX and volatility measures involving standard deviation, variance and ATR. The lesson offers two distinct execution branches: a breakout after a mature range, and a rejection/fade from a range boundary. These should not be merged into one rule that simultaneously buys a breakout and fades it.

The baseline uses Volatility mode, range period 14, multiplier 1.8 and a five-bar cooldown. SL/TP display is enabled with TP multipliers 1, 2 and 3.5 and SL multiplier 0.8. Additional narrated inputs are ADX threshold 25, smoothing 14, standard-deviation multiplier 0.8, variance 0.7 and ATR 0.9. The formula underlying the SL/TP multipliers is not explained, so they are not automatically 1 R, 2 R, 3.5 R and 0.8 R.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Identify the exact Zeiierman script/revision and reproduce the stated baseline on the same type of data before evaluating alternatives. Save all actual inputs, including the selected detection mode.
2. Breakout branch: wait for a range lasting roughly 8–10 bars, seek supporting volume, require a candle to CLOSE outside it and enter at the NEXT candle’s open according to the narration. Use the plotted stop/target levels only after confirming their calculation and availability.
3. Fade branch: at the boundary, look for the stated rejection evidence—doji, wick or a volume spike without follow-through. The lesson prefers ADX below 20 here, places the stop just outside the boundary and aims toward the middle or opposite side. Define a precise pattern/trigger before testing.
4. The lesson suggests hourly/four-hour range agreement as confluence; determine what is known before the four-hour bar completes.
5. Keep alternative presets separate: forex period 20/multiplier 2.2; crypto 10/2.5 with Volatility mode only and TP 3 multiplier 5; gold 25/1.5 with both detection methods mentioned. Log each as a distinct candidate rather than tuning per outcome.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The video does not disclose full formulas, whether range boundaries freeze, repaint behavior, data warmup, the base unit behind every TP/SL multiplier, partial allocations, a volume threshold or account risk fraction. A close outside a range and next-open execution can produce gaps/slippage different from the colored drawing. The fade branch’s just-outside stop also needs a numerical buffer.

TP2 and TP3 checkboxes are unchecked in the reviewed target panels despite the claim that all three targets are calculated/displayed. The extra 337 s frame shows TP3 value 5 with its checkbox off, and SL value 1 rather than the narrated baseline 0.8. 27–80 s introduces detection components;84–145 s gives baseline settings;173–215 s explains breakout close/next-open entry;220–249 s explains fade;261–278 s discusses MTF;307–352 s gives alternative market presets. Source: [ZynAlgo](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1Hr4KDLZLF/). Downloaded duration: 14.766 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

ZynAlgo’s music-backed advertisement opens TradingView’s script search and selects Scalper Pro v 4.1, with similarly named test scripts also visible. It then points at buy/sell markers on selected charts, colored position regions and a dashboard. The repeated caption says the creator deleted every other indicator. A performance panel shows profit factor 4.23 with a GOOD label. This demonstrates the advertised interface and sales claim, not a transparent strategy or independently verified trading record.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Preserve the exact version and author identity; v 4.1, v 4[Test] and a Kalman/VWMA-named result are not automatically the same implementation.
2. Save the actual inputs and market/feed before comparing signals.
3. Record when a fresh buy/sell label and its entry/stop values become available in replay, then compare with the final historical chart.
4. Define order timing, sizing and exit handling independently if documentation does not supply them.
5. Recompute performance from a complete trade log, including losers, fees, spread, slippage and any open position.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The clip does not reveal the underlying algorithm, full settings, repaint behavior, test interval, position sizing or exact dashboard methodology. Profit factor is a gross-profit/gross-loss ratio, not a win rate, and a displayed 4.23 does not establish future or executable profitability. The chart pointers highlight favorable moves and provide no denominator of all signals. The claim of replacing every other indicator expresses preference, not comparative evidence. No purchase or account connection is necessary to document this limited demonstration.

Original 0–2 s frames show Scalper Pro v 4.1 and similarly named scripts; later charts show selected buy/sell markers; approximately 12.5 s dashboard shows Prof.Factor 4.23 GOOD.

# Developing session POC shifting with price and value area

Source: [Anand I SEBI Reg RA](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1KuGn8TZoU/). Downloaded duration: 5.04 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Anand’s poster follows the point of control as the current session develops, rather than using only a finished profile. Its bullish checklist combines a POC shifting higher, price above POC, a value area building higher and higher highs accompanied by a higher POC. The bearish checklist reverses those relationships: lower POC, price below it, lower value area and lower lows. The early-to-late-session drawing depicts new volume accumulating at higher prices and moving the highest-volume bin upward.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Define the session and start a developing profile using only volume available so far.
2. Save the POC and value-area boundaries at each decision timestamp.
3. Compare their movement with price; evaluate the full bullish or bearish checklist rather than treating a single one-tick POC change as a complete order.
4. Define how much change and how much persistence count as a consistent shift.
5. Add the entry trigger, invalidation, objective and risk policy separately before testing directional continuation.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The poster gives no session calendar, feed, bin resolution, value-area percentage, change threshold or observation interval. There is no stop, target, size or rule for POC ties and abrupt jumps between near-equal bins. A POC shift is not the same as every trade migrating smoothly upward; the winning bin can change discretely. The image’s fair-value/magnet language describes a hypothesis about historical participation, not intrinsic value or guaranteed attraction. A final session POC must never be used as if it had been known during the early session.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

All original static frames show Developing POC Shift, early/developing/later session profiles, both directional checklists and the magnet/fair-value claim.

## What it does

DanFord demonstrates a two-handed kettlebell movement called the Deadman Gravedigger. # Integration plan: EMA and structural-break continuation entries, with an unspecified adding policy

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `d01f68bfcbe6ccb96ca8efd6ff8b7a1ab98ca2a57c1afd539f537bf543587029`.

## Experiment overview

FinShala with Priya shows a static bearish chart headed EMA + BoS. Successive lower breaks establish the pictured direction; a 50 EMA crosses below a 200 EMA, and two later pullbacks toward the moving averages receive first-entry and second-entry labels. A faster green curve is also drawn, but its period is not established. The written recipe combines structure for directional context, an EMA crossover for confirmation and pullbacks for entry. It then proposes adding positions until structure breaks in the opposite direction.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Evaluate the particular setup or indicator sequence described here on a frozen historical universe. First produce causal features and candidate events; promote it to a trade simulation only after the unresolved entry, invalidation, exit and sizing decisions below have an explicit versioned specification. A daily-equity adaptation must be labeled when the source uses another interval or product.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to use or reproduce it

1. On a fixed instrument and timeframe, identify the swing lows whose downward breaks would count as bearish BOS. Preserve those levels before the break.
2. Add the visibly identified 50 and 200 EMAs and observe their bearish crossover. The chart illustrates confirmation after the decline has already begun.
3. Mark the subsequent pullbacks and their rejection areas around the averages. The arrows illustrate short continuation locations, not a fully specified order trigger.
4. Treat the later entry as a separately recorded additional position. If researching the source's adding idea, set a total exposure cap and per-position invalidation before any order.
5. Specify which opposing structural break ends the thesis; the sheet does not supply executable stop or exit prices.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Reuse EMA50/200 and causal structure-break features, keeping the unnamed faster curve unresolved. Every addition needs its own trigger, position cap and cumulative risk accounting; the initial entry does not authorize unlimited pyramiding.

**Indicators:** [analysis/rule_catalog.py](../../analysis/rule_catalog.py) and [analysis/rule_engine.py](../../analysis/rule_engine.py) supply typed indicator operands/comparisons; [analysis/indicator_engine.py](../../analysis/indicator_engine.py) supplies MACD, SMA, Wilder RSI and other series. Match formulas before reuse: rsi() is rolling-mean RSI, rsi_wilder() differs, and atr() uses span EMA rather than Wilder ATR. [indicators/_math.py](../../indicators/_math.py) has Wilder ATR/EMA/DEMA building blocks. Stateful sequences or missing formulas need a dedicated adapter rather than forced Builder conditions.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Warm EMA200/50 and confirmed structural references; obtain the unnamed faster curve before selecting its startup window.

Use the longest selected rolling/recursive dependency plus prior-value comparisons and confirmation delay. Treat indicator NaNs as not-ready; never backfill initial values from later bars. Keep each market/interval series independent.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

**Indicators evidence:** Export feature values and each condition’s pass/fail reason. Test exact numeric fixtures, cross equality, recursive seeds and constant-price/zero-variance cases. Compare individual filters before the combined stack.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and evidence limits

No price source, timeframe, swing algorithm, candle-close requirement, exact pullback depth, protective stop, target or position sizing is provided. The unnamed faster curve must not be silently assigned a common default. Keeping additions open until an opposing BOS is not a complete loss-control rule and can increase aggregate exposure. The selected uninterrupted decline does not establish the crossover's predictive accuracy or the profitability of pyramiding.

**Practical next step:** Write and approve a small explicit research specification resolving the source gaps above, then validate numeric/event fixtures and a short causal replay before a full historical run. Missing rules should block the faithful trading mode; a labeled feature/event study may be the practical first milestone.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

# Four kettlebell combinations for arms, forearms and grip

Source: [Frameofdavid](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1DWSvjcHsT/). Downloaded duration: 12.027 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Frame of David presents four simultaneous exercise demonstrations rather than trading content. The saved caption names around-the-world into curl, curl into pullover, reverse curl into upright row and kettlebell clean. The aim is arm and grip training with one kettlebell, mixing controlled elbow flexion, a higher pull and a more dynamic clean. The video is a brief visual menu, not a real-time recording of an entire workout. The four panels run together, so the viewer should study each separately rather than attempt to copy all four sequences at once.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Around-the-world → curl: the first panel passes the bell around the body, then brings it forward for a curl. Learn the hand-to-hand pass separately and keep the curl controlled rather than using the pass to fling the weight upward.
2. Curl → pullover: the second panel uses a two-handed hold for the curl and a movement around/above the head. This is the creator's standing pullover combination, not a demonstrated supine bench pullover; the short cut does not establish every part of its range.
3. Reverse curl → upright row: the third panel raises the bell with an overhand-style grip and then brings the elbows higher for the row. Distinguish the two actions and lower under control.
4. Clean: the fourth panel brings the bell upward toward a front-held position. The short view should not substitute for learning the clean's timing and grip transition.
5. The caption prescribes 8–15 controlled repetitions per exercise, 3–4 rounds, with 60–90 seconds of rest as needed. Start with a comfortably controllable load. Keep curls strict and stop the cleans if speed, balance or technique deteriorates. The caption explicitly advises learning movements separately before combining them.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

Bell weight, unilateral repetition counting, exact rest placement, weekly frequency and progression increments are unspecified. The caption's rep range and rounds are the creator's proposed dose, not an individualized prescription. The twelve-second montage does not demonstrate completing that volume, prove a particular muscle-gain rate or establish suitability for every shoulder or training history. Its membership and starter-plan promotion adds no movement mechanics. There is no financial strategy to implement or evaluate here.

## Local evidence and reproducibility

Original frames 0.00 seconds, 3.40 seconds, 6.79 seconds and 10.19 seconds show the four exercise panels and changing positions. # Control wicks: lower-price rejection versus upper-price rejection

Source: [Ghulam fareed Trading acedemy](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1dSMm91uMf/). Downloaded duration: 10.005 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Ghulamfareed uses a hand-drawn candle sheet to contrast a buyers-control wick with a seller-control wick. The left sequence highlights a long lower shadow beneath a relatively small candle body; the right highlights an upper shadow after green candles. The caption's practical distinction is that lower wicks represent rejection of lower prices and upper wicks represent rejection of higher prices. The dashed boxes isolate the wick regions rather than defining a chart-wide support or resistance zone.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Read the candle's open, high, low and close before labeling a wick. The body spans open to close; the remaining high/low extensions are shadows.
2. For the left example, note the excursion below the body and the recovery before the candle closed. Describe that as lower-price rejection within this bar.
3. For the right example, note the upper excursion and closing position beneath the high. Describe that as upper-price rejection within the bar.
4. Record surrounding trend and any pre-existing level separately. A wick alone does not establish which larger structure remains intact.
5. If turning the observation into a study, choose a minimum wick/body ratio, a location filter and a later confirmation rule before inspecting the outcome. These are additional research decisions, not supplied entries.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The sheet supplies no instrument, timeframe, size ratio, entry, expiry, stop or target. Buyers control and seller control are teaching labels: OHLC candles do not identify participants, remaining orders or who will control the next bar. A bullish candle can have an upper rejection wick and a bearish candle a lower one. The noisy machine transcript is not reliable enough to add numerical rules beyond the visible graphic and caption.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

The complete hand-drawn sheet is legible in original frame 07 at 9.85 seconds: the lower boxed wick is labeled Buyers Control Wick and the upper boxed wick Seller Control Wick. Earlier samples show the same comparison being pointed out.

# Triangle breakout trap followed by a separately confirmed bearish branch

Source: [The Alpha Trader](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1eqwxMb4Ea/). Downloaded duration: 19.966 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Alpha Trader animates a triangle-like consolidation after an upward move. A novice buys the first upper breakout; the example then shows an upper liquidity sweep and a return into the formation. A later downside break and retest receive a sell label, with a short risk region above and an objective below. The intended lesson is to wait for structural confirmation instead of treating the first penetration of a diagonal boundary as a guaranteed continuation.

1. Draw the consolidation boundaries from swings already known before the potential break. Preserve the preceding trend as context.

# Integration plan: Market Structure and Break order blocks with a 0.273 Fib Factor

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `b06b1e00fdf89a211f645557adbe1b533a413fe5616ec5b0d2c0bfc67550b5b6`.

## Experiment overview

TRADINGCHART demonstrates the Market Structure and Break indicator and edits its Fib Factor before illustrating green order-block regions. The narration proposes a long bias when more than one green block is present, an entry above the block nearest current price and a three-to-one reward/risk objective. The word safe in the narration is an opinion about that selected configuration, not a measured probability or guarantee.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Start with a specification/prospective-signal capture study. The shown tool, selected recap or undisclosed model does not yet define a reproducible trading engine. Obtain its exact revision, inputs and as-issued signals before enabling a faithful performance run; a public-formula proxy must have a separate experiment identity.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to use or reproduce it

1. Identify the exact Market Structure and Break script/author and freeze its revision. The name is not enough to reproduce an independently modified version.
2. Open Inputs. The shown ZigZag value is 9; the final Fib Factor is 0.273. A temporary 0.33 during editing is not the final setting. Show ZigZag and Delete Old/Broken Boxes are enabled in the displayed setup.
3. Wait for the required count of green blocks and identify the nearest one using information available at that moment. Save its original bounds before it is touched or deleted.
4. The spoken entry is above that nearest block. Establish whether this means a resting order, rejection close or another precise trigger before testing.
5. The suggested target is 3R. An initial protective stop must first be defined to calculate R; the source does not fix that boundary.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Preserve ZigZag9 and final Fib Factor.273 as the script’s structure-break setting. Do not use .273 as a retracement entry or probability. Obtain exact box lifecycle and retain broken/deleted zones in results.

**Swings:** [patterns_v2/patterns/common.py](../../patterns_v2/patterns/common.py) exposes causal ZigZag pivots with separate pivot and confirmation indices; [core/rsi_divergence.py](../../core/rsi_divergence.py) demonstrates evidence carrying pivot/confirmation dates. Reuse these timing ideas only after matching the writeup’s own swing hierarchy. Add a dedicated structural event/zone ledger where the source calls for it.

**Zones and gaps:** Propose a stateful zone/gap adapter with origin, first-known, active, touched, invalidated and expired timestamps. [patterns/011_breakout_retest.py](../../patterns/011_breakout_retest.py) offers a price-break/retest reference but does not implement a universal order-block/FVG specification. Freeze the writeup’s wick/body boundaries and trigger sequence before reuse.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Retain prior structural levels and enough bars for right-side pivot confirmation. A level’s origin date and first-known date differ. Missing prior swings make the setup ineligible; do not pick future extrema to complete a pattern.

Retain the zone-formation/impulse history before the chosen date range. A three-candle gap becomes known only after its third candle; a block validated by later displacement becomes available only after that validation. Missing formation history makes it unavailable.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

**Swings evidence:** Log pivot origin and confirmation, protected-level updates and every failed or stale candidate. Change bars after a decision and assert identical prior levels/signals. Backdated chart labels must never become backdated fills.

**Zones and gaps evidence:** Export original zone bounds, formation/availability, every return and invalidation. Test early touches before zone availability, overlapping zones, no-return moves and failed retests. Do not treat institutional-order narratives as OHLCV-observed facts.

For the initial incomplete-specification state, report the missing dependencies and any captured configuration/signal evidence; trading metrics remain unavailable. Product slogans, floating P&L, dashboards and selected chart rectangles are not validated performance.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and evidence limits

Timeframe, swing confirmation delay, complete box construction, entry buffer, stop, sizing and expiry are missing. ZigZag pivots can become known after their plotted turning point. Deleting broken boxes can remove unsuccessful historical candidates, so evaluation must archive them as they originally appeared. Several stacked green regions do not establish independent confluence or make a trade safe; the example supplies no complete outcome series. The position tool visible at 25.27 seconds displays about 2.67 reward/risk, which differs from the spoken 3R suggestion; the example must not be reported as an exact executed 3R trade.

**Practical next step:** Obtain the exact script/model revision, complete inputs/formulas or lawful timestamped as-issued signals, and its entry/exit/size contract. Capture changing-bar and repaint behavior prospectively. Until then, keep the faithful performance run disabled; use an explicitly named proxy only after specifying its differences.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.
