# Five-movement kettlebell circuit, with an unsupported spot-fat-loss claim

Source: [Will Bedard](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1KV2Ca6jXq/). Downloaded duration: 25.1 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Will Bedard demonstrates a kettlebell circuit labeled oblique drops, kneeling chops, around-the-worlds, swing press and overhead raise. The caption prescribes ten repetitions of each movement, three to five rounds, no rest between movements and keeping the bell off the ground throughout the sequence. These are the creator's proposed workout parameters. The clip's claim that rotating the core gets rid of love handles should not be treated as a demonstrated physiological result.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Oblique drops: the bell is held at one side while the torso moves laterally, then returns. The short view does not establish range, load or repetitions per side.
2. Kneeling chops: the labeled section uses a kneeling/half-kneeling setup and a two-handed diagonal bell movement. Learn this position separately rather than inferring it from the standing exercises before and after it.
3. Around-the-worlds: pass the kettlebell around the body, changing hands. The original sample shows the bell beside the hip; this is not the same action as an overhead halo.
4. Swing press: study the transition from the lower bell position toward the upper pressing position as its own skill. The clip provides no detailed timing or loading instruction for that combination.
5. Overhead raise: the final section raises the bell above the head with two hands, then returns it downward. The standing overhead movement is distinct from the kneeling chop.
6. If documenting the advertised dose, record ten reps per named movement and three to five rounds. That is 50 named-movement reps per round before any unresolved left/right counting. Rest between rounds, bell weight and weekly frequency are not stated.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The no-rest/continuous-hold instruction increases fatigue demand; a short edited demonstration does not establish whether the full dose is appropriate for an individual. Repetition counts per direction or side are ambiguous, and the video does not supply a progression plan or technique assessment. Core work does not selectively remove fat over the trained area: the American Council on Exercise rejects spot reduction in its [fitness-myth explanation](https://www.acefitness.org/about-ace/press-room/press-releases/319/ace-lists-most-common-fitness-myths/). Thus the exercise menu and the promised local fat-loss outcome should be evaluated separately. This is fitness content and supplies no trading method.

## Local evidence and reproducibility

Original samples 0.00–24.95 seconds show the five labeled movement sections; 7.13 seconds shows the kneeling chop, 14.26 seconds the bell around the hip and 21.39 seconds the standing overhead raise. The full caption supplies ten reps, three to five rounds, no inter-movement rest and the bell-off-ground instruction. The spot-reduction correction is supported by the linked ACE primary source.

# Order-block validity: imbalance, forceful departure and nearby liquidity

Source: [Rohit Prasad](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1HckZkMZe7/). Downloaded duration: 52.08 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

## What it does

Rohit Prasad defines an order block as the last opposite candle before a move that breaks structure, then gives three conditions for treating a block as valid: a related FVG/imbalance, strong momentum away from the area and nearby liquidity. The Hindi narration rejects a slow or weak departure. The example develops from a prior decline into a bullish structural shift, a marked demand/order-block region, imbalance, a return and a higher target. It is a qualitative filtering lesson rather than a complete trading algorithm.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Identify the structural break and the last opposing candle associated with its impulse. Do not label every opposite candle an order block without the departure/BOS context.
2. Check the source's first condition, an FVG/imbalance associated with the block. The narration's with/inside wording does not precisely define overlap or which candles establish the gap.
3. Assess the departure's strength. The source contrasts a forceful impulse with a weak, slow movement but supplies no numerical displacement threshold.
4. Mark the nearby liquidity reference, such as clustered prior highs/lows. Its distance and eligibility need an explicit definition in any implementation.
5. Apply all three as filters, then study the later return to the zone. The long illustration and upper target show the intended direction, not an exact universal trigger or R multiple.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

Timeframe, body-versus-wick zone boundaries, swing scale, overlap threshold, momentum measurement, liquidity distance, stop, size and expiry are unspecified. These conditions can be correlated manifestations of the same price move rather than three independent signals. Neither a fast departure nor a subsequent reaction proves institutional inventory. Validity must be determined with information available before entry and tested against failed blocks as well as this successful illustration.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Complete narration spans the 52.08-second file. Original samples 0.00–51.92 seconds show the order-block definition, rejection of weak movement and the FVG/momentum/liquidity checklist with a bullish retest/target example.

sources.overview: Abdokofficial explains a bearish break-and-retest setup. A structure break is required; without one, the narrator says there is no trade. After the break, price should return to the broken level and reject it. The proposed short uses the retest area, a stop above the high and a target at the next support. This source provides relative entry, invalidation and objective locations, while leaving their numerical implementation open.
sources.gaps: The source omits timeframe, swing hierarchy, break/rejection threshold, stop buffer, size and maximum retest wait. Its target is structural, not an expressly fixed R ratio. Price can retest several times, gap through a stop or reach support without filling the chosen entry. Statements implying the method works every time remain unverified. Good entry placement affects the available risk distance; it does not make the direction certain or prevent a loss.

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `23e4005b8f2a665a625a38c863097fdc186437c383e7982276cf5dad8c47498b`.

## Experiment overview

Alphaalgotrading shows a five-minute GBP/USD OANDA chart with an AlphaAlgo buy, green cloud and several upper take-profit levels. A dashboard changes its buy counts/states as the chart advances. The ending selector identifies AlphaAlgo. This is a separate example from the creator's BNB/USDT short: the symbol, venue, direction and market context are different even though the promotional layout is similar.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Start with a specification/prospective-signal capture study. The shown tool, selected recap or undisclosed model does not yet define a reproducible trading engine. Obtain its exact revision, inputs and as-issued signals before enabling a faithful performance run; a public-formula proxy must have a separate experiment identity.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to use or reproduce it

1. Match GBP/USD, OANDA and the five-minute interval shown. Keep the selected feed distinct from exchange-traded currency futures or another broker's candles.
2. Record the AlphaAlgo script's exact author, revision and full input set. The brand is not the same as the independent AlgoAlpha creator.
3. Capture the initial buy label, cloud state, entry/stop references and all upper target prices before revealing later candles.
4. Archive the dashboard counts as they evolve. Values such as 6/15 or 9/15 need a definition of the counted conditions; they are not automatically success probabilities or completed profitable trades.
5. Specify whether the targets are partial exits, alternative objectives or merely visual levels. A reproducible result requires explicit quantities and a rule for the remaining position.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Create a source-specific adapter for the sequence in the Rules and inputs section, preserving the order in which each illustrated reference and confirmation becomes known. Store candidate, armed, confirmed, expired and invalidated events separately. [patterns/base_pattern.py](../../patterns/base_pattern.py) supplies signal/annotation structures, while [indicators/_signal.py](../../indicators/_signal.py) demonstrates latest-bar output; neither supplies the missing source rules. A recap or undisclosed indicator stays blocked until its actual generator and execution specification are available.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. Missing specifications/data should produce explicit preflight blockers.

[core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

**Source interval constraint:** This writeup includes intraday/tick or hourly branches. Select any source-supported daily branch explicitly; the following constraint applies to the finer-interval branches. Daily OHLCV cannot reconstruct its internal ordering, session windows or lower-frame confirmation. The owner has local hourly loaders but the history API has no hourly route, and hourly bars cannot recover one-/five-/fifteen-minute or tick data. A faithful branch remains blocked until a suitable historical source and remote access contract exist. Any added daily-bar equity adaptation needs a separate identity and explicit changed rules; do not present it as the original experiment.

**Instrument constraint:** The source example’s non-equity instrument/feed or contract is not automatically in the US/PH stock-history universe. Check actual symbol/market coverage and preserve price units, sessions and any contract multiplier. An equity/ETF proxy is an additional research hypothesis, not an equivalent dataset.

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

For the initial incomplete-specification state, report the missing dependencies and any captured configuration/signal evidence; trading metrics remain unavailable. Product slogans, floating P&L, dashboards and selected chart rectangles are not validated performance.

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and evidence limits

No signal formula, complete settings, bar-close convention, initial stop policy, target allocation or size is supplied. The caption's nonrepainting implication is not established by scrolling a finished chart. Multi-timeframe information and the current candle may still change before close. The selected favorable move and multiple TP labels do not prove that all targets were filled at their displayed prices or establish net account performance.

**Practical next step:** Obtain the exact script/model revision, complete inputs/formulas or lawful timestamped as-issued signals, and its entry/exit/size contract. Capture changing-bar and repaint behavior prospectively. Until then, keep the faithful performance run disabled; use an explicitly named proxy only after specifying its differences.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

# Integration plan: AMD phase mnemonic across sessions and days, with a duplicated candle row

Source: [writeup.md](writeup.md). Planning only: this document proposes future integrations and does not implement a tab, strategy or engine. Source snapshot SHA-256: `bc4916c461ef51ddc8c9fb5014b7cb2315135b612b34157c6742bc8bc5acc8a2`.

## Experiment overview

ForexLogix presents an accumulation/manipulation/distribution mnemonic rather than a worked chart trade. The Time row maps Asia to accumulation, London to manipulation and New York to distribution. The Day row maps Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday to those phases. A third row is headed Candle but repeats Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday instead of supplying candle-specific definitions. That visible inconsistency is part of the source and should not be silently repaired into a different three-candle strategy.

**Proposed evaluation scope:** Start with a causal annotation or filter event study of the described condition. Measure all qualifying cases and compare a separately frozen entry model with and without that condition. A descriptive label or selected reference picture is not automatically an order.

## Rules and inputs

**Evidence boundary:** The source interpretation below retains the writeup’s own wording, including its qualifications, corrections and explicitly added research examples. A numbered procedure can contain a proposed operational choice; it is not automatically a rule attributed to the video. No unstated timeframe, conventional default, mirrored trade or numerical stop/target becomes source-backed through inclusion here.

### Writeup: How to use or reproduce it

1. Transcribe the two clear mappings as hypotheses about session/day context, not as guaranteed classifications of every market period.
2. Define a market, named timezone, session boundaries and daylight-saving handling before studying the session version. Asia/London/New York alone do not supply precise windows.
3. Give accumulation, manipulation and distribution observable price criteria. The slide offers names and sequence, not measurable range/displacement thresholds.
4. Preserve the Candle row as unresolved because its weekday labels duplicate the preceding row. Additional source material would be needed to explain what three-candle pattern was intended.
5. If developing a trading study, add an independent trigger, invalidation, objective and exposure policy. None follows automatically from knowing which day or session it is.

**Experiment input contract (proposed):** timestamped open, high, low, close and volume, market/session identity, versioned source interpretation and all declared parameters. Additional datasets and source-specific dependencies below are mandatory only for the branch that needs them. A signal-only study can proceed once its event definition is complete; trade P&L additionally requires explicit entry/fill, invalidation, exit and sizing policies.

## Proposed integration

Create a source-specific adapter for the sequence in the Rules and inputs section, preserving the order in which each illustrated reference and confirmation becomes known. Store candidate, armed, confirmed, expired and invalidated events separately. [patterns/base_pattern.py](../../patterns/base_pattern.py) supplies signal/annotation structures, while [indicators/_signal.py](../../indicators/_signal.py) demonstrates latest-bar output; neither supplies the missing source rules. A recap or undisclosed indicator stays blocked until its actual generator and execution specification are available.

The future Experiments page would extend [web/app.py](../../web/app.py) and [web/templates/base.html](../../web/templates/base.html), using Paper’s [template](../../web/templates/paper.html) and `initPaper` in [web/static/app.js](../../web/static/app.js) for US/PH controls, status, tables and chart inspection. Add experiment selection, start/end dates, parameters, requirements, Start/Cancel and saved results. Use [web/static/backtest_runs.js](../../web/static/backtest_runs.js), [web/runs.py](../../web/runs.py) and [core/backtest_jobs.py](../../core/backtest_jobs.py) as lifecycle references: background execution, run IDs, polling/reconnect, loading/warm-up/session progress, cancellation, errors, interrupted runs and explicit retry.

Propose a versioned catalog and typed contracts in `core/experiments/`, source-specific adapters and `web/experiments.py` (new components, not existing APIs). Register this directory’s source ID/digest; requests freeze market, inclusive dates, parameters, universe/data hashes and execution policy. A proposed `/api/experiments/catalog` and `/api/experiments/runs[/{id}]` flow would validate requirements → load → warm up → replay → persist/poll results, with a run-specific cancel action. [core/backtest_service.py](../../core/backtest_service.py) offers frozen-input/artifact contracts but is currently coupled to pinned pattern versions; extend or wrap its lifecycle rather than assume an arbitrary-strategy plug-in API. [core/stream_backtest.py](../../core/stream_backtest.py) demonstrates a growing causal store, pending next-open fills, warm-up without orders and explicit end policy; [core/rule_backtest.py](../../core/rule_backtest.py) is a simpler rule-replay reference. Audit their detector, sizing and exit contracts before reuse. Keep experiment state separate from live Paper books and the immutable pattern registry. Paper’s DII/Kronos/Laya gates and loss/trailing/exposure policies apply only when explicitly selected as experimental assumptions. Durable run storage and history-owner routing are separate deployment concerns.

## Data handling

Determine warm-up from the longest declared indicator, reference range and formation window, plus prior-value comparisons and pivot confirmation delays. Retain pre-start zone/anchor state when required. If the source leaves these windows open, finalize them before declaring a minimum; insufficient history produces a per-symbol not-ready reason, not fabricated values.

Use [docs/daily-bars-api.md](../../docs/daily-bars-api.md) and [data/history.py](../../data/history.py): snapshot `list_history_symbols(market=...)`, then `load_daily_bars(symbol, market=...)`. When `STOCKS_HISTORY_URL` is empty and the process owns history (`STOCKS_HISTORY_OWNER` or existing deployment/host detection), `local_history_backfill_enabled()` selects local PostgreSQL `stocks_history` through `data/db.py`. Otherwise the existing authenticated `data/history_client.py` uses the history HTTP API; `enable_ui_web_history()` supplies the remote default for a non-owner web process. Preserve that routing in workers, with existing credentials and no silent CSV/Yahoo/TradingView fallback.

Snapshot each market’s available symbols, optionally narrowed by explicit tickers; current membership/delistings and corporate-action adjustments are unverified. PH keys use `.PS` through `core.market.ph_history_symbol`. Use `core.market.get_market` for separate USD/PHP reporting, New York/Manila session calendars and PH long-only eligibility. Report unsupported short branches explicitly; do not invent a long mirror. Freeze costs and use tick/lot helpers with the historical `as_of` date where relevant.

Validate start ≤ end; filter inclusively by market-session `date`/`bar_date`, retaining `ts` identity. The facade offers exclusive `after_ts` and newest-N `limit`, with no end-date bound. Fetch enough pre-start history (or all history), then filter locally; newest-N can omit an old interval entirely and bulk’s 2,000-bar cap is not historical pagination. Pre-start bars only warm features/state. Sort/validate completed, finite OHLCV and conflicting/duplicate sessions; preserve missing sessions and zero/missing-volume status. Higher-frame context must use completed calendar periods.

`None` from `load_daily_bars` means failure; `[]` means no bars. Preserve this distinction before candle/frame conversion and report insufficient warm-up separately. Symbol enumeration currently collapses remote errors to `[]`: propose an explicit failure status before treating an empty universe as success. Bulk helpers can return partial maps after chunk failure; reconcile every requested symbol, retry missing keys and bound concurrency/cancellation. Surface auth/transport/503 errors without exposing credentials. No history ingestion or repair is part of an experiment run.

## Results and validation

Freeze interpretation, parameters and execution before testing. Expose only completed decision bars and prior data to the adapter; close-generated signals fill no earlier than the next tradable open. Limit/stop orders become eligible only after their conditions are known. Preserve pivot confirmation, external publication and higher-frame availability times. Test prefix invariance by changing/removing future bars and requiring unchanged earlier features, signals and orders. Use raw market prices for fills, keeping synthetic Heikin-Ashi/regression prices as features.

For fully specified trades, report candidate/accepted/rejected/expired/unfilled counts, trade and signal/fill timestamps, rule/level evidence, fees/slippage, net expectancy/R where defined, win rate, profit factor, realized/unrealized P&L, marked-to-market equity, exposure, turnover and drawdown by market. Compare a frozen baseline with identical dates/universe/costs; label independent-notional versus finite-capital accounting. Without entry/exit rules, report event coverage and predeclared forward-return/MAE/MFE horizons or forecast calibration, leaving trading P&L unavailable. Outcome windows never enter features and are censored at end_date with incomplete horizons reported.

Use fixtures alongside [core/test_stream_backtest.py](../../core/test_stream_backtest.py), [core/test_rule_backtest.py](../../core/test_rule_backtest.py), [core/test_backtest_service.py](../../core/test_backtest_service.py) and [web/test_paper_api.py](../../web/test_paper_api.py): source positives/near-misses, date boundaries, warm-up without orders, missing/invalid data, owner/remote parity, `.PS` and market isolation, enumeration/auth/partial-bulk failures, progress/cancel/retry and valid no-signal runs. Declare gap-through-stop and conservative same-bar stop/target ordering; daily OHLC cannot reveal intrabar order. Freeze end-date treatment (mark open positions or labeled liquidation), with last-bar orders unfilled if no later eligible bar exists. Use untouched later holdouts and retain all trials, failures and costs.

## Gaps and assumptions

### Writeup: Missing rules and evidence limits

No instrument, chart interval, timezone, phase-confirmation rule, entry, stop, target or statistical sample is supplied. Sessions do not invariably follow the proposed sequence; labeling a price excursion manipulation does not prove intent. The caption's career-change anecdote and free-PDF invitation add no missing mechanics. This clip is a conceptual phase map with an apparent copy error, not an executable calendar-based signal.

**Practical next step:** Agree one causal annotation/event definition and audit it against hand-labeled examples with future bars hidden. Only then attach a separately specified entry/exit baseline and test whether the condition adds value.

**Proposed assumptions, not source facts:** the experiment catalog/API paths, adapters, daily-stock adaptation, warm-up/seed conventions where unspecified, next-open execution convention, costs/slippage, sizing, finite-account policy, same-bar ordering and end-date handling are design proposals. Keep source-established values and unresolved alternatives in separate manifest fields. Claims of institutional activity, guaranteed moves, AI confidence or advertised profitability require independent evidence; OHLCV labels alone cannot establish them.

Fxflowreels provides a static three-way classification of market behavior. Its uptrend sketch says Buyers > Sellers, its downtrend says Buyers < Sellers and its range says Buyers = Sellers. The practical tip is to trade a clear trend and hold cash during a range. This is a directional-context lesson, not a demonstrated entry, risk or exit strategy.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Classify the visible price path over a declared timeframe and swing scale. A rising sequence, falling sequence and sideways interval are the pictured categories.
2. If implementing the idea, choose a consistent definition such as confirmed swing progression or a measured slope/range threshold. Those numeric choices are additional research rules; the sheet supplies none.
3. Treat the inequality captions as shorthand for directional buying/selling pressure. Every executed trade has matched buying and selling, so the diagram does not literally count more transacting buyers than sellers.
4. Define what clear trend means before deciding that a new entry is permitted. Preserve ambiguous transition periods rather than relabeling them after the next move.
5. The hold-cash tip concerns avoiding new range trades; the source does not specify whether it also closes an existing position or how that position would be managed.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

No instrument, timeframe, trend threshold, entry trigger, stop, target, sizing or evaluation is shown. A market can trend on one scale and range on another; the classification needs a fixed scope. Trend-following still has failed signals and reversals, and avoiding ranges may exclude profitable breakouts. The graphic cannot establish which regime would have been knowable in real time or quantify a benefit from its filter.

SwiftAlgo UG advertises Swift Algo X on an OANDA EUR/USD one-minute chart. The montage shows selected buy/sell annotations, colored risk/reward regions and take-profit labels. The content demonstrates the tool's visual presentation rather than exposing its forecasting or signal formula.

1. Record the displayed Swift Algo X identity, version, provider and complete inputs before trying to reproduce its output.

The clip omits the full algorithm, input set, signal confirmation, repainting behavior, stop updates, size and complete outcome history. # ScalperPro v4.1 across gold and NAS100, with an expectancy dashboard

Source: [ZynAlgo](https://www.facebook.com/share/r/1A9uHQZFvr/). Downloaded duration: 12.538 seconds. The source is a lesson or demonstration, not independently verified performance evidence.

ZynAlgo shows ScalperPro v4.1 [ZynAlgo] first on XAUUSD five-minute and later on NAS100 fifteen-minute charts. Colored long-trade regions and selected continuation moves are accompanied by a dashboard with market-type, trend/EMA, ADX, RSI, volume and entry/stop information. An expectancy display changes around 0.86R–0.89R. The montage shows multiple instruments using a product layout, not an independent multi-market study.

## How to use or reproduce it

1. Preserve ScalperPro v4.1, its full inputs and each instrument/feed/timeframe separately. Do not merge five-minute gold and fifteen-minute NAS100 into one supposedly uniform strategy without an explicit rule.
2. Capture the signal and associated entry/stop/target region before future bars. Record whether the dashboard describes trend or sideways conditions at that time.
3. Obtain the definition and underlying trade sample for expectancy. Establish which trades, revisions, partial exits and costs the displayed R calculation includes.
4. Specify how EMA/ADX/RSI/volume conditions affect eligibility. Their dashboard presence alone supplies no numeric thresholds or priority.
5. Evaluate every eligible signal on later data, preserving failed trend labels and trades excluded by any regime filter.

## Missing rules and evidence limits

The algorithm, complete settings, entry timing, risk size, target allocation and raw trade history are withheld. An expectancy number is a claim about an unspecified sample, not a guaranteed future average. No independent calculation validates 0.86R or 0.89R, and the display may change with the visible chart/history. Selected successful gold and index moves do not establish robustness, nonrepainting operation or executable profits after costs.


## Local evidence and reproducibility

Original samples 0.00–12.35 seconds show ScalperPro v4.1 [ZynAlgo], XAUUSD 5m followed by NAS100 15m, selected long regions and the market/indicator/expectancy dashboard. The expectancy readout is retained as an unverified displayed statistic.

# SPECTRA Signal Processing Engine on fifteen-minute QQQ

## What it does

1. Preserve the video and identify the displayed SPECTRA - Signal Processing Engine [SentioEdge] script. Obtain its revision and complete input export before claiming an exact reproduction.
2. Match the displayed QQQ and 15-minute interval, then identify the actual feed and colored line calculation. The visible name and timeframe alone do not reveal the algorithm.
3. Save any original signal, step-line level and risk/reward region with its issue time. A monitor recording of a finished chart does not establish when the historical marks first appeared.
4. Determine whether line color, line crossing or a separate label is the proposed entry; the video does not choose a mechanical trigger.
5. Add initial stop, exit/target, quantity and signal-conflict rules before evaluating outcomes. Keep hypothetical chart regions distinct from submitted orders.

The original legend establishes the script identity, but the clip supplies no complete formula, input set, bar-close timing, repainting test or full trade ledger. The drawn favorable region is not a verified fill or account result. Calling the indicator brutal is marketing emphasis and establishes neither a statistical edge nor a rule for losses, gaps and failed signals.

Original samples 0.00–15.18 seconds show the filmed monitor, step-like colored line and green/red trade regions. The 2.17s original frame identifies SPECTRA - Signal Processing Engine [SentioEdge], QQQ and 15m. Full settings remain undisclosed.
